Its click on "Properties" now takes the blueprint's page, not the first of that name (the Module panel's, or before it the toolbar's): the item's Properties page view draws 11,860 vertices against the baseline's 14,754: the baseline's click had taken the old toolbar's Module Properties, so that view's numbers before T2 were another view's, and its numbers from the T2 run (`m3-t2-frame_perf.log`: 1.75 ms CPU idle, 11,860 vertices) are its baseline from now on. The five T2 timing logs are kept in `target/ui-mock/perf-m3/t2/` (not in git) for later tasks to compare with.

**T2's fix round, 2026-11-12** (after its review). (1) Undo: the fallback to the side editor in front of the focused pane made the module's Undo unreachable from the Top Bar after work in the tree (an empty hak's window focused left the button and Edit › Undo grayed while Ctrl+Z over the tree undid the module's step), or took a hak's step instead. The fallback is now the active editor, the one the user last worked in: `Moonglow::note_worked`, after the dock is drawn, notes a pointer press or a key away from the Top Bar and its menus (a press on a side editor's body or tab makes it the active editor; anywhere else, the module; a key is the 2DA grid's with the keys, unchanged while a text field is focused, else where the pointer is; read from the frame's raw events, since the keymap has taken Ctrl+Z by then), and `side_doc::worked_side_editor` takes it only while the editor is open and its tab in front of its pane. The rule as built, with the pointer on the Top Bar or a menu open (button, Edit › Undo and Ctrl+Z alike): come straight from a side editor, that editor's (`undo_before_bars`, unchanged); else the editor last worked in, if still in front; else the module's. Over a side editor, Ctrl+Z is the editor's; elsewhere, the module's (unchanged). An editor with no steps of its own still grays them (the side editors' rule of 2026-10-21). Tests: `shell.rs`'s `undo_on_the_top_bar_is_the_active_editor_s` (replacing `..._falls_back_to_the_active_side_editor`), `..._after_an_area_is_the_module_s`, `..._with_a_floating_editor` and `..._after_the_talk_table_is_its`, each asking by the button, Edit › Undo and Ctrl+Z and checking that the three say the same. (2) The Status Bar's right-hand items share the room left after the Log switch by one rule (`shell::share`): the game folder goes first; then the module's name and the note of a look under way ("Reading files changed outside Moonglow…") are cut short with an ellipsis, each to half the room where both are wider, or to what the other leaves; the note's words and the name's path in their tips, " (modified)" kept whole (the kit's `StatusItem::kept` and `max_width`, with `shown` and `is_cut`). A kit test, a unit test of the sharing, `a_long_module_name_is_cut_short_in_the_status_bar` at 420, 600 and 1000 with and without the note (`Moonglow::show_looking_note`, hidden, sets it for tests), and `screens.rs`'s `shell_long_name` (`shell_long_name_note_420.png` too). (3) The Top Bar's groups go in order as the window narrows: both are decided after the menus are laid out, the quick actions where they fit, the build actions only where both do (`the_top_bar_drops_its_build_then_its_quick_actions_as_the_window_narrows`, 300 to 1400 by 20). (4) The main window has a least inner size, `mg_ui::LEAST_WINDOW_SIZE`, 420 by 320 points: the menus end about 395 points from the left, as many points at every interface size, and a size kept smaller opens at it (`at_least` in `apps/moonglow`, on the builder eframe gives with the kept size, in points that egui-winit makes pixels at the zoom eframe restored). While Moonglow runs, `shell::keep_least_size` gives the least size again (`ViewportCommand::MinInnerSize`, in points, which egui-winit turns into pixels at the frame's scale) each time the scale changes once the interface size is in effect (Options › General › Interface size, Ctrl with + and -, a screen of another scale), and grows a window smaller than it in points (`InnerSize`). Tests: `at_the_least_window_size_the_menus_fit` at each size Options offers (`mg_ui::UI_SCALES`, 90% to 200%), `the_least_size_follows_the_interface_size` (the commands sent as the setting changes, and the window grown at 300%), and `a_window_kept_smaller_than_the_least_size_opens_at_it`; what a window manager does with the commands needs a display and was not run.

**Done, 2026-11-12.** The Module panel is `tree::module_tree` under the Left Dock's tab bar (`shell::left_dock`). The tab bar carries the panel's four header buttons after the Module tab, in the board's order: **Module Properties** (the `module` cube, as its row: the board's `properties` sliders are drawn as Area Properties' icon, and an icon is one command's, `icons::an_icon_is_one_command_s`), **New Area** (`plus`), **Expand All**, **Collapse All**, then the fold button (beside the dock's edge since T4). Expand All and Collapse All are the tree's (`palette_view::fold_icons`, its keys unchanged) and reach the tree the same frame through `module_tree`'s new `fold` argument. The header button and the tree's row named Module Properties are told apart by group and role: the button is in the "Left Dock" group, a button; the row is in the "Module Tree Rows" group (inside "Module Panel"; "Module Tree" was the View menu's row, "Left Dock" since T4's fix round), a selectable label. The Filter is the board's: the `filter` icon, the placeholder "Filter" (`SearchField::icon`), and Clear Filter, in a `.panel-bar` margin of 4 and 8 px; the tree's rows reach the panel's sides. Each group's row is the kit's new `mg_uikit::TreeGroup` (`mg-uikit/src/tree.rs`, with `TreeRow` for a row that opens nothing): 22 px, the chevron in a 14 px column, the kind's icon, the name 42 px in, the count against the edge in sight (6 px in, kept there when the tree scrolls sideways), hover `hover-row`, marked `accent-fill`. It keeps egui's collapsing state under the same id and keeps the accessible name "Areas (113)", said expanded or not, so no test that finds a group changed. An area's kinds of placed objects (R2, kept) are `TreeGroup`s too, with the kind's icon, and "3 of 46" under the Filter; a kind with nothing placed is a quiet `TreeRow`; Module Properties and the "N other resources" line are `TreeRow`s. A resource row, an area's row and a placed object's are the kit's `TreeRow` too: the name 36 px from the panel's edge (22 into the group's rows, after the arrow's column, as the board's), the fill across the whole row from the panel's edge, an area's arrow a button of its own in the arrow's column. **The Areas group scrolls in a well of its own** (`areas_well`): a vertical and sideways `ScrollArea` as wide as the tree's view, pinned there when the tree scrolls sideways, taking its height alone in the tree's layout, with a height of the tree's whole view (a scroll bar across its foot or not) less one row for each of the tree's other rows (Module Properties, each group shown, the line under them), in whole rows, at least the board's five, and no more than its rows. The board gives no rule but draws the same arithmetic: its Module panel of 496 px is the tabs, the filter, two rows, five in the well and thirteen groups. With the groups closed, every group is in sight under Areas in an 800 px window (Chapter1, 113 areas: 14 rows in the well), and the well is not resizable. Rows out of sight in the well are not laid out (the tree's culling works on the well's clip). The tree's keys, selection, Filter and follow-the-tab logic are unchanged. Only `bring_into_view` and `reveal_into_view` learned of the well: a scroll area works out a row to scroll to by the part of itself in sight (none, with the tree scrolled past the well) and keeps the target from the tree around it. So inside the well they leave the row (`well_target`), the well scrolls itself to it after its rows are laid out (to the middle, or only as far as needed, as before), and the tree brings the well into its view. Home and End over the well go to its top and foot, and elsewhere over the tree to the tree's. Differences from the plan and the board: the board shows no module-wide count, so the "N resources" beside Expand All is gone (each group's count and the "N other resources" line remain); New Area's tip says "Make a new area with the Area Wizard" and Module Properties' "Open the module's properties"; the Left Dock's least width is 190 px (`LEFT_DOCK_LEAST`, from 150), so its tab bar's controls never overlap, also in the least window; the folded strip is T2's, unchanged, and shows the Module panel alone until T4 adds Resources. **Fix round, 2026-11-12.** A review of the commit found five faults, which this round fixed, each with a test in `tests/app/module_panel.rs` and pictures before and after (`target/ui-mock/impl/m3-t3-fix/`, not in git). (1) The well was laid out as wide as the tree's view, and the tree keeps the widest it has drawn (`tree-widest`), so a Left Dock widened and narrowed again scrolled 322 px sideways into nothing, with a scroll bar that took a row from the well: the well takes its height alone in the tree's layout (`Ui::new_child`, as the kit's rows take only the width their words need) (`a_narrowed_dock_leaves_the_tree_no_wider_than_its_rows`, `shell_tree_narrowed`). (2) The well's place, kept for Home and End, outlived the well: once the Areas group closed, Home and End did nothing where it had been. It is known for the frame the well is drawn in and only within the tree's view (`home_and_end_go_to_the_well_s_ends_over_it_and_the_tree_s_elsewhere`). (3) A word typed in the Filter and cleared brought the well back at its top, and a word that finds nothing did the same to the tree: the well scrolls under an id of its own while the Filter has something typed, and the tree's place before the Filter is put back once it is cleared (`the_well_and_the_tree_keep_their_places_through_the_filter`). (4) Resource rows' fill hugged their names and the names stood 40 px in: they are now `TreeRow`s (above), for which the kit gained `TreeRow::sense` (a blueprint's row drags), `arrow_apart` with `tree::arrow_column` (an area's arrow is its own button, before the row, so that it keeps its clicks, its tip and the keyboard's focus before the row's; the row answers from its name on), `fill_under` (the row's fill under that button) and `show_parts` (where the marks after the name go: the claims mark and "(not in the area list)", not selectable, so that a click on them is the row's); a row's fill reaches the left edge of the scroll area it is in (the board fills an indented row's indent), and the arrow of a marked area row is drawn on the fill in `on-fill` (`a_tree_row_fills_the_row_drags_and_leaves_its_arrow_to_a_button` in the kit; `shell_tree_rows`). (5) The well dropped a row when another group opened: the tree's scroll bar (8 px) came from (1), and the well now measures the tree's whole height, so a sideways bar that is needed does not change it either (`the_well_keeps_its_rows_whatever_else_is_open`). The review's other asks: the menu test opens the menu of a row in the well and of the rows cut at its top and foot, waiting for them rather than counting frames, and says that nothing in the well drags (an area's row and a placed object's are clicked, not dragged; the drag tested is a blueprint's under the well, the well scrolled, so the auto-scroll at the well's edge has no row to try); the tab test chooses the tab with Ctrl+Page Up and a click on it; new tests hold the five-row floor and a three-area module's three rows, every group reached in the least window by the wheel and the keys, F2 and the Rename window on an area in the well (there is no field of the tree's own: Escape closes the window and leaves the well, Enter renames), Delete on one (the well as high and where it was), a tab's menu's Show in Module Tree for an area deep in the well and a script under it, F6 and Shift+F6 out of the tree and back to a row in the well and Tab from it to the next row, and Shift and Ctrl choosing across the well's border. **Done, 2026-11-12.** Quick Open is `crates/mg-ui/src/quick_open.rs`, the Top Bar's middle (`shell::top_bar_row` hands the kit's slot to `quick_open::middle`; `quick_open::after_bar`, called by `Moonglow::ui` right after the Top Bar, draws the popover and does what was chosen). **The field**: the glass, "Go to resource or command", the key cap of the key actually bound (`Cmd::QuickOpen`, id `quick-open`, Ctrl+P; none where it is unbound; said as the field's description), at most 440 points (300 under W 1300), named "Quick Open". A click, typing or the key opens it (bare focus by Tab does not, so Tab passes through to the build actions); Ctrl+Shift+P and Help › Command Palette… (the same ids) open it with `>`, which restricts it to the commands (SPEC names no other prefix). **What it finds**, one list best first: the module's resources (by ResRef, and an area's or a blueprint's name, as the Module panel's Filter; the objects placed in an area, which the Filter also looks through, and tags are not matched), then the commands (`commands::found(app)`, every row the palette had: the menus' commands, plugin commands and entries, project commands, grayed where they cannot run, a tip saying why: `Id::why_disabled`), then the load order's resources (the game's, haks', override's, the module's own layer left out; they open as the Resources panel opens them: `browser::tab_for`). The rule, in the module's comment and held by unit tests: equal, then prefix, then a word's start (after a character that is no letter or digit), then anywhere, then every word apart, then (commands only) with the menu's name; at one tier a name match before a ResRef match, then the shorter name, the name and the ResRef alphabetically, and of one ResRef the file with an editor first (a script's source before its compiled form). At most 50 rows (`MOST`); a line under them, always in sight, says how many more ("N more: type more to narrow them"), and "Indexing…" while the index is made. Each row: the kind's icon, the name, a dim detail (the ResRef and type of a named resource, a command's menu, a load-order resource's layer, a recent module's folder), a command's key cap. **Empty field**: the module's recent areas (`Settings::recent_areas`), most recent first, still in the module; recent modules' areas are not offered (they cannot be opened without opening their module); with no module open, the recent modules (opened as File › Recent Modules opens them, asking about unsaved work) and the commands that work without one. **Keys**: Down and Up move the choice with wrapping, Page Down and Page Up a page (stopping at the ends), Enter runs it, Tab stays in the field while it is open, Escape closes it and gives the keys back to the widget that had them (recorded in `keys_pressed` before a typed-in field gives them up; a pane's arrow keys are untouched, so the area view keeps its keys), and keeps a dialog under it open (`widgets::keep_escape`). A press outside closes it running nothing; a press on it is neither the area view's nor work in an editor under it (it lies on a Foreground layer); the areas opened lately are named at once where the index has not come to them, and frames are asked for while it indexes, none at rest. While the field has the keys it is a text field as any: a key that types is its (a command given a plain letter waits); a key with Ctrl or a function key runs its command (Ctrl+S saves the module, as in any field) and closes Quick Open. A job closes and grays it. **Ctrl+P and a builder's own key**: `Keymap::give_way` (called by `Keymap::new` and after plugins' and projects' keys are taken in) leaves Quick Open without Ctrl+P where another command that works at the same moment was given it by the user, a plugin's manifest or a project's file, unless the user chose Quick Open's keys too (then both have it, a conflict in Options as usual); the key it gives up is recorded as its own for the while, so the settings never keep it unbound. **Yields** (taken from T14, local to the Top Bar): the field narrows with the room the bar leaves it, is capped at 300 under W 1300, and becomes an icon button (the glass, "Quick Open", its key in its tip) where it would be under 240; then the build actions go, then the icon, then the quick actions. Under the icon (or with no room at all, as at 420), the key and the icon open the field over the bar's middle (300 wide at most, inside the window) with the same popover. **The index**: made the first time Quick Open opens; the module's part again when the workspace's revision, its count of resources or its file changes (`ModuleStamp`), names taken 2 ms a frame (`BUDGET`) where the window works in the background; the load order's part again when `Moonglow::load_order` moves and its layers but the module's (label, fingerprint) changed, made on a thread in the application (it holds the game data only while it reads, about 200 ms). The load order's resources are searched as one text (`Game::find`, with `memchr`'s `memmem`, already in the tree through aho-corasick): on the game with TDoD's 150 haks (382,394 resources, a 1-minute load of 8 on this machine) the index takes about 200 ms and its search at most 1.9 ms ("a", 138,306 found), 0.08 to 0.3 ms for longer queries; a whole keystroke there with Chapter 1 open (the popover's rows made, commands and all, nothing narrowed from before) 2.1 ms for "a" and 0.19 to 0.44 ms for the rest; Chapter 1's module part 0.7 ms, its names 43 ms in all; a made-up module of 50,000 named resources 1.1 to 1.6 ms a keystroke (searched entry by entry), so a first one-letter keystroke on both would be about 3 ms. The load order's part holds about 55 MB for those 382,394 resources once Quick Open has opened (an estimate from the entries' size, not measured). At rest Quick Open draws its field and nothing else. **Gone**: the modal `commands::palette_window`, `commands::Finder` and `Moonglow::command_palette`. **What builders notice**: Escape closes at once (the palette's first Escape cleared what was typed); a key with Ctrl runs its command while typing (the palette held every key back); `>` with nothing after it shows the first 50 commands and how many more (the palette listed every one); a command's detail is its top menu. (2) The load order's part had kept only the copy the game reads, so a game resource one module overrode was missing in the next: it is now made of every layer but the module's (the highest copy of each), a resource the module has too shown once, as the module's (a bit set per load-order row, worked out when the module or the part changes), and kept across a generation whose layers but the module's are the same. Where the keyboard is: the widget that had the focus as the last frame ended (`focus_was`, its place read at the Escape alone, `Moonglow::keyboard_at`, when egui has taken the focus already, so the read changes nothing of it; a focus moved by Tab counts), else the last press (`last_press`). M4 (each editor's change): the Creature and WideCreature boards' 3D view hints (Drag Turn view, Right Drag Move view, Middle Drag, Wheel, Shift + Wheel) to the blueprints; the script's "Line 17, column 12" count and the Script board's 170 cap to the script editor; the Conversation board's hints and "3834 words" to the conversation editor; the Table and Talk boards' hints and counts ("6 cells", "840 rows, 59 columns", "112228 lines") to the tables; NUI, Tileset, Hak ("2706 resources, 183.8 MB", "3 selected"), Journal and Factions boards' to the rest; GalleryPalette's and AppearanceGallery's (and "838 appearances") to the galleries; the Resources board's counts at the bar's right (its count stays in the panel) to the rest; the gizmos' readout chips beside the drag hints to the gizmos; the viewer's boards to M6.

**Review, 2026-11-13.** An independent review of T12 (its commit `148485e2`) found, and this round fixed: (1) **Enter: OK shown where Enter does something else**: with the module tree holding the keys (a press on the Left Dock, F6) and the pointer over docked Options, the bar said Enter: OK while the tree takes Enter first (`tree.rs`'s `consume_key`). Enter's hint now takes the same exclusion as the Esc hint, `palette_view::a_list_has_the_keys` (the module tree, the Resources panel, the log); `docked_options_hints_enter_where_it_is_ok` holds it (the tree's keys, nothing focused: no Enter, and Enter leaves Options open); broken, "never: no Enter, the tree's keys". (2) **Two Esc guards whose tests could not fail**: the "menu open" step clicked View, so the pointer and the last press left the tab and the hint went for that reason. `esc_hint` now opens the tab's own menu (a right click on its tab, nothing focused, the pointer over its body; Escape closes the menu, the tab stays) and holds the module tree's keys with nothing focused (asserted); broken alone, the popup guard gives "never: no Esc hint, the tab's menu open" and the list guard "never: no Esc hint, the tree's keys" (both modes). The review saw the list guard pass when broken because the tree's keys came with egui's focus; in this tree after F6 nothing has the focus (now asserted), and the break failed at the commit too: the test's press on the Left Dock before F6 is what lets the pointer's rule reach the tab. A dropdown of Options open is no case of the popup guard alone: it takes the keyboard (egui's focus), so neither Esc nor Enter is hinted for that reason, which the Options test holds. (3) **A floating model's window under the pointer**: an Escape closes it (`tabs::Viewer::body`'s `model`, no check of the docked tab seen), so the docked tab the keyboard is in is not canceled; the hint now goes where the pointer is over such a window (`Moonglow::model_under_pointer_next`, set where `body` computes `model`). Of the windows' paths, it is the one that takes Escape whatever a docked tab saw: a window in front with OK and Cancel takes it only where no docked tab did, dialogs and menus are the guards already there. `a_model_window_under_the_pointer_takes_the_esc_hint[_as_tabs]`: the last press in Module Properties, the pointer over a model's window, no hint; Escape closes the window, the tab stays; broken, "never: no Esc hint, the model's window under the pointer". (4) **The area's hints while they cannot act**: the view's keys and presses need `response.hovered()`; a modal (a job's window, `egui::Modal`), a dialog (Resize Area) and an open menu each kept Q from turning the selection with the pointer over the view (measured), so `shell::keys_blocked` (any of the three) clears the area's hints, the counts kept. With the pointer elsewhere in the window the hints stay (they say what the view's keys do); the manual (02, 04) says the area's keys act with the pointer over the view. `nothing_in_front_or_no_area_hints` (menu, dialog, modal; back after each); broken, "never: no hints, a menu open: [\"Drag: Move\", …]", and without the modal, "never: no hints, a modal in front". (5) **The readout during a drag**: the old line read the selected object from the area's model, not the posed one a drag moves (`AreaView::posed`), so it showed where the object was before the drag, not live; it was visible at rest, though, which "1 selected"'s tip is not. Now while one object is dragged or turned (a drag, or Q and E's turning) its kind, tag, blueprint, place and facing lead the hints as a note, read from the posed model as it moves; at rest it stays "1 selected"'s tip, as GizmoStates draws "1 selected" (its mid-drag hints are Esc, Middle Drag and the snap, and its chips on the view are M4's gizmos'). A note at the hints' head, not an item at the right: the readout changes each frame of a drag, which the right-hand items do not, and the GizmoStates board's mid-drag notes ("Snap 0.5 m") are in the hints. `the_object_moved_reads_where_it_is`; broken, "the place read as it moves: []", read from the model "…: [\"Waypoint NW_WAYPOINT001 (nw_waypoint001) at 20.00, 20.00, 0.00, facing 107°\"]", and without Q's "read while Q turns it". (6) **Smaller untruths**: the ring's Turn and Q, E Turn by a step now show only where something selected turns (`turns`: not a sound), Alt + Drag Raise only where something selected is not a creature (they stand on the ground). With the ring on, Alt + Right Drag still turns, but the Main board draws the ring alone for a selection (Main-status draws Alt + Right Drag for nothing selected, where it does nothing): the ring alone is hinted, decided by the board. Broken, `the_other_area_states_show_their_hints` gives "never said [\"Drag: Move\", \"Alt, Drag: Raise\"] without [\"Turning ring: Turn\", …]" and "never said [\"Turning ring: Turn\", …] without [\"Alt, Drag: Raise\"]". (7) **The cost claim**: each hint was measured three times a frame and `shown` made twice; now the kit's `Hints::measure` gives `MeasuredHints` (width, fit, drawing from one measure) and `shown` is made once a frame after the editor area (`shell::update_shown`; `Moonglow::status_said` returns what it made). Measured (`shown_cost_on_a_large_area`, release, `perf-m3/t12/review_cost.log`, load about 7): on 549 objects (area084's count) the making takes 0.0011 ms with nothing selected, 0.0020 with all 549 selected, 0.0015 with Shift held; the fullest hint set's frame 0.074 ms against 0.062 without (`hints_cost`). (8) **Tests and pictures**: `the_other_area_states_show_their_hints` covers a sound alone, a creature alone (and Shift: Tilt, Scale), Ctrl + wheel's scale, a static placeable's refusal for its four seconds (the window's own time, 3 to 5 s), pasting objects and tiles, Redraw Polygon, placing an appearance, a trigger and a door, a tile brush over an object and Select Tiles' notice first; broken, the refusal never going and the brush's note gone each fail it. The Resources test's last step asserts Module Properties' hints by name. The Light pictures now include `shell_welcome`, `shell_wide`, `shell_status_hints_*` and `status_bars_area_states`. Also: `tiles::a_brush_s_tiles_are_drawn_by_the_game_s_shaders` waited 40 frames for the game's programs and failed once under load; it waits with a deadline (half a minute) for them to be made, and, the programs withheld (Moonglow's shader), fails "the area's tiles, by the game's programs". `area_view.rs`'s `area_viewer_places_draws_boxes_and_turns` read the bar's "Placing nw_waypoint001" one frame after choosing the blueprint; the bar now shows it a frame later still, so it waits for it with a deadline. Disagreed with and said: the readout was never live (finding 5's wording); the list guard's test did fail when broken at the commit (finding 2), though it is now independent of focus by assertion.

**T13. The Outliner (R2, ruled).**

- **Goal.**

- **Files.** New `outliner.rs` (reuse the tree's per-area contents code, `tree.rs` contents and row helpers), `shell.rs`.
- **Tests.**

- **Manual.** 02 (new Outliner section), 04-areas.

**T14. How the shell yields, and the wide layout.**

- **Goal.** Apply `Yields` (section 5.2):

**Done, 2026-11-14.** **Plan against board** (the boards won where they differ): (1) Narrow.png's strip has a chevron at its top; the strip kept T5's button beside its edge instead (one control, where the fold button was: T5's ruled-out chevron, issue 10's rule), the three icons below as the board has them. *Changed by the review below: the chevron at the strip's top, the open dock's button at its tab bar's end.* (2) Neither the boards nor SPEC say what unfolding does in a narrow window: decided, it pushes the editor area as at any width (no overlay) and holds while the window is under the width that folds the dock; from there the builder's own fold has it, so a window narrowed again folds it again; `hide_tree` and `hide_palettes` are never written by it. **Review, 2026-11-14.** An independent review of T14 (its commit `d6b04e1f`) found ten faults; each is fixed with a test seen to fail with the fix taken out (the failure text in brackets). (1) **Show in Module Tree did nothing visible at the app's first size** (1280 by 800, the Left Dock folded by the width): it set the reveal and the panel but never unfolded the dock. It goes through `show_dock_panel` now (`set_dock_open`), as Tools › Resource Browser, Palettes and Preview do. Audited, every command that asks a dock's panel on purpose: Show in Module Tree, Tools › Resource Browser, Tools › Palettes, Tools › Preview, the strips' buttons and chevrons, View › Left Dock and Right Dock and their keys unfold the dock; the tree and the Resources panel reveal rows only within a drawn dock (the tree's following and the browser's keys); no command opens the log on an error; Quick Open and Find Instance open tabs or go to the area, asking no dock; the plugins open no dock panel; a blueprint chosen in the palette shows in the Preview only where its dock is drawn; the Outliner's reveal is within its drawn dock. `module_panel::show_in_module_tree_from_a_tab_s_menu_reaches_into_the_well_and_below` now folds the dock in its 1000 window before each Show in Module Tree ["the dock unfolded"]; `yields::a_panel_asked_for_by_name_unfolds_its_dock` (1280 and 700). (2) **The tests' hook hid the default user's layout**: `docks_fold_by_width` is gone, the yields on in every harness. No test turns the yields off now: UI tests unfold the Left Dock as a builder would at 109 places in 25 files (its strip's chevron, `common::unfold_left_dock`, some of them in shared set-ups that more tests go through), those that read or write the builder's own fold run in a 1600 window at 20 places (`common::wide_window`), the Right Dock is unfolded at 7 (`unfold_right_dock`), and `screens.rs` unfolds by hand at 11 places, the 9 cases the hook had served among them; the app's 1338 tests (34 ignored) pass with the yields on. Faults the migration found in the product: (1) above, (5) and (10) below; and in the tests, `common::click_tab_close` could take another tab's close square once a dock folded (it takes the rightmost one in the tab now). (3) **The keys and a dock not drawn** (the orchestrator's decisions, reversible on the owner's word): (a) when a dock holding the arrow keys is folded, by the width or by hand, they go to the editor area's active editor (`shell::keys_leave_folded_docks`, `Moonglow::editor_keys`) and are not handed back when it unfolds; (b) F6 moves only among what is drawn: it no longer unfolds a dock folded by the width (the one-way unfolding and, under 962, the layout flipping at each round, are gone); a folded dock's strip buttons are reached by Tab and named, and View's rows and their keys unfold it. `yields::keys_leave_a_dock_that_folds` ["the editor's with the dock folded by the width: left: \"Tree\" right: \"Area\""]; `yields::both_docks_where_they_do_not_fit_and_f6` [with the unfolding put back: "F6 never unfolds it: [\"Palette\", \"Log\", \"Tree\"]"]. #### Part 5. Decided

Decided by the implementer on 2026-11-11:

- **U1.** Wide layout from W ≥ 2560: Left Dock 320 by default, Right Dock two columns when wider than 560.
- **U2.** Replace README's `area.jpg` at M3c (the shell picture changes then); the editors' screenshots at M5.
- **U3.** Each dock keeps one fold control (issue 10's rule): for Left and Right, open, a button at the end of the dock's tab bar (the Left Dock's at its bar's end toward the editor area, after the Module panel's buttons; the Right Dock's at its bar's end by the window's edge, after its tabs, and in the wide layout's two columns at the end of the last column's bar), and folded, the chevron at the strip's top (T14's review and second review); the Status Bar switch for Bottom.
- **U4.** The Status Bar shows the module's name and "(modified)", the path in the tip.
- **U5.** Existing settings keep the Log open; new installations start closed.
- **U6.** No dragging panels between docks in M3 (ruled by the owner as R5).
- **U7.** Ctrl+Shift+P opens Quick Open restricted to commands.
- **O5.** `mg-uikit` takes egui_dock 0.21 behind an optional `dock` feature, so that the viewer gets the dock style and tab marks from the same place: ruling 9 put the shell in the shared crate. The crate's "egui alone" comment is changed with it.
- **Merge points.** M3 is merged into `develop` at three points, M3a, M3b and M3c, each coherent with the manual true.

#### Part 6. Rulings for M3

Put to the owner on 2026-11-11 with a recommendation each, and ruled the same day: "You may proceed as suggested." Each is carried out as its recommendation says.

- **R1 (the plan's O1). Escape on a docked tab with OK and Cancel** (a Properties tab, Options). Today Escape cancels only a floating one (`tabs.rs:393`), so As Tabs takes it away from new users, and the Options board's hints omit it (proposal finding 13.4). **Ruled, as recommended:** Escape cancels the active docked tab that has OK and Cancel while the pointer or keyboard is in it, as floating does; the hints then show Esc. Gates T10.
- **R2 (O2). The module tree's area rows opened out to their objects, once the Outliner exists.** The boards' Module panel lists areas without arrows; the moves tables do not say. **Ruled, as recommended:** keep both in M3 (builders rely on "the tree follows the selected object", and its tests are many); decide the removal with M4's area editor. Gates T13. *Note, 2026-11-14:* the following moved to the Outliner by the owner's ruling in T13's review ("Yes: while the Outliner shows, the tree stops following the selection"): the tree keeps its areas opened out when the builder opens them, and follows the selection only while no Outliner shows.
- **R3 (O3). Plugin panels** (`Tab::PluginPanel`, Plugins › Panels) as editor tabs or windows, following the switch, or as Right Dock panels. **Ruled, as recommended:** tabs or windows in M3 (they are not one editor's); revisit when the dialogs become panels in M4. Gates T10.
- **R4 (O4). Retiring "Toolbar buttons" at M4, not M3**, since the area toolbar's Icons-only mode is what keeps it on one row until M4's header. **Ruled, as recommended:** yes, at M4. The Top Bar ignores the setting from T2 and the Options control is renamed until then. Gates T2's Options wording only.
- **R5 (new, from U6 with T4 and T5). Panels are fixed to their docks in M3.** Today the resource browser and the palettes can be dragged to a side or into the middle and are docked there (GitHub issues 10, 11, 20 and 23, the `docs/deferred.md` entries named in T4 and T5); with the docks as panels that goes away: Resources lives in the Left Dock, Palette and Preview in the Right Dock, and a dock folds but its panels do not move. **Ruled, as recommended:** accept it for M3 and M4 (the mock's shell places every panel, and no board shows a panel moved), and file moving panels between docks as its own later piece of work only if the owner wants it. Gates T4 and T5; tasks before them (T0 to T3) do not depend on it.

#### Handing out the tasks

A standing note for whoever hands out the tasks:

- One code writer at a time in the worktree.
- After each task, an independent read-only reviewer on the commit, then a fix round.
- The owner's findings from live testing M2 take the writer's slot ahead of M3 tasks.
- The hand-run timing tests (`frame_perf`, `editor_perf`, `world_perf`, `campaign_perf`, `nui_perf`) are run after any task that renames or moves controls, since the suite only compiles them.

**Planned in detail, 2026-11-14.**

M4 is the largest milestone of the redesign: every editor's insides change, and with them the docks learn to hold what each editor brings. Cut into tasks of one to two days of an agent's work it is 31 tasks, U0 to U30 (U: T is M3's), about 57 days of work, three and a half times M3's 16. About 500 test lines migrate (the area toolbar's lookups, about 110 lines through `common::area_tool`; the blueprint pages clicked by name, about 130 lines, through one new helper; the 25 lines that set "Toolbar buttons" or the area's hidden tools; Tile Properties' OK and Cancel; the script's and the conversation's panes where a test runs As Tabs), and about as many are added. The owner's word of 2026-11-14 holds: M4 lands on `ui-redesign` task by task and goes into `develop` once, at its end, after asking. Seven facts frame the plan:

- **Tests run floating, and a floating editor keeps its panels.** `Settings::default()` is As Floating Windows (M3, Part 2, decision 4), and a floating editor draws its own side and bottom panes inside its window (decision 3; the Floating board draws exactly that: the script's Reference and Help at the window's right, Compiler, Bookmarks and Search Results under its text). So each panel's body is one function with two hosts, the dock when the editor is docked and in front, the editor's own pane when it floats, and most of the roughly 1,344 UI tests keep passing as they are; each task adds As Tabs tests for the docks.
- **An editor's state already lives outside its window.** The views are kept on `Moonglow` by document (`scripts`, lib.rs:681; `dialog_views`, :730; `model_views`, :893; `area_views`, :904), so a dock panel reads the active editor's state by its key. The docks are drawn before the editor area: a panel shows what the editor left the frame before (as the Status Bar has since T12), and a panel that draws a 3D view the editor may also draw is drawn late, in the room the dock kept (the Preview's `preview_slot`, area_tools.rs:786-800).
- **A placed object's Properties already apply at once.** `blueprint::ok_cancel`'s contract (blueprint/mod.rs:320-327): "what was changed is the module's already"; OK closes, Cancel sets back the window's changes as one Undo step. The Properties panel (S2, ruling 2) is therefore `edit_many`'s body without its OK and Cancel, not a new way of editing.
- **The kit has none of M4's parts yet.** `mg-uikit` has the metrics (`EDITOR_HEADER` 30, metrics.rs:32; `TOOL_SHELF` 36, :36; `TOOL_BUTTON` 28, :38; `POPOVER_RADIUS`, :53) but no header row, popover, More, tool shelf, page list, footer row, step list or gallery cell. Its `shell::Yields` already carries the area header's three yields (`header_compact`, `value_text`, `into_more`), which nothing in `mg-ui` reads yet. What it has and M4 reuses: `segmented` (controls.rs:136), `Join` (icons.rs:347), `IconButton::menu`, `PanelHeader` (shell.rs:951), `DockTabs`, `TreeGroup::eye` (tree.rs:440), `TreeRow::second` (:573), `KeyCap`, `Badge`, `Hints`, `StatusSwitch`.
- **The order has one constraint the paragraph below does not show.** The Problems and Search Results panels come, by the paragraph, with "the dialogs that become panels" at the end; but the script editor's Search Results (U13) and the tileset editor's Check (U20) need them earlier. So the Bottom Dock learns to hold several panels, each with its Status Bar switch, in U2, and each of the two panels arrives with its first feeder (no switch without a panel, M3's S3); the dialogs fill them in U28.
- **"Toolbar buttons" goes when its last reader does (R4).** Six toolbars read it (`icons::Tools::of` at script_view.rs:755, dialog_view.rs:1095, model_view.rs:1229, nui_view.rs:876, hak_view.rs:733; `Tools::of_area` at area_view.rs:3092). Each editor's task stops reading it for its own toolbar; the setting, its Options control and its draft go in U23, after the hak editor (U21), the last of them, and with the Options page that the board draws without it.
- **Code is read with agdb** (`trail` is retired). Every task ends as M3's did: `cargo test --workspace --exclude mg-corpus-tests --lib --bins --tests`, the three clippy commands, `cargo fmt`, where docs changed `okf index docs`, `okf lint docs --links` and a `docs/log.md` entry, an agdb note for what the code cannot tell, the task's pictures rendered with `screens.rs` before and after in both themes (`MG_LIGHT=1`) into `target/ui-mock/impl/m4-uN/`, and the hand-run timing tests after any task that renames or moves controls (the suite only compiles them).

Four merge points, review and stability points on the branch (none goes into `develop`), each coherent with the manual true and the task's moves rows ticked:

- **M4a, after U8**: the area editor as the Main, Narrow, WideArea, AreaPaint, AreaTiles, Floating and GizmoStates boards draw it (header, popovers, tool shelf, compass, Paint and Tiles states, Tile Properties and Properties panels, the Right Dock's sections, the handles).
- **M4b, after U15**: blueprints (page list, columns, Preview panel), the script editor and the conversation editor, each with its panels docked and floating.
- **M4c, after U24**: the tables and the rest (NUI, tileset, hak, journal, factions, the read-only resource, Options, Welcome); "Toolbar buttons" retired.
- **M4d, after U30**: the shared gallery cell, the pickers, the dialog pattern, the dialogs that become panels, the closing pass; then the owner is asked to merge into `develop`.

#### Part 1. How today's editors are built (what the tasks change)

Checked against the code on 2026-11-14. "OK and Cancel" below is `blueprint::ok_cancel` (blueprint/mod.rs:328) or `side_doc::ok_cancel` (side_doc.rs:157), both drawing `ok_cancel_saying` (blueprint/mod.rs:338-368): a bottom panel, OK then Cancel at its left, Close alone when read-only. No editor draws them at a header's right end today.

**The area editor.**

- The toolbar is `area_view::toolbar` (area_view.rs:3088-3434, called at :3004), one `horizontal_wrapped` (:3104) named "Area toolbar" (:3107). In order: a "Show X" toggle per kind (:3109-3120), Start, All, None; Night, Lighting, Shadows (`shadows_button`, :4498), Fog, Fade Geometry (`lead_dropdown`, :4334), Animations, Grass, Tile Border, Shaders, Grid, Minimap, Play Sounds, Sound Ranges, Ambient, Music; Snap and Turn dropdowns, Together, Onto Objects; Walkmesh… (`walkmesh_button`, :4436, a menu); Select Tiles and Paint (disabled read-only); Area Properties; Reorient Camera (:3381, inline, not a command); Go to Start Location (:3386; also `Id::GoToStart`); To Scratch; "Save N as Prefab…" (several selected); last the warnings "problems" and "N missing" (:3420-3436). Paint's second strip follows it while Paint is on (`paint_mode::strip`, paint_mode.rs:1011-1104: Scatter, Row, Fill, Erase; Radius, Density, Count All, Spacing, By Size, Flow, Turn, Scale, Gap, Height, Lock by mode; "N chosen").
- The strip's right-click menu (:3098-3103) is `toolbar_menu` (:4381-4433, also on Options › Area, options.rs:1001), which writes `Settings::hidden_area_tools` (settings.rs:820); `Tools::of_area` (icons.rs:248) folds it with `toolbar_icons_only` into a mask over `AREA_TOOLS` (icons.rs:181, 29 names).
- There is no Terrain mode and no compass. Terrain brushes are the tiles palette's (`terrain_mode::palette_ui`, terrain_mode.rs:1621-1800); the minimap is drawn at the view's top right (`minimap_overlay`, area_view.rs:3878-3935, placed at :3861), where the boards put the compass (the minimap goes to the bottom right).
- Select Tiles' commands are its right-click menu (`tile_select::context_menu`, tile_select.rs:521-572) and keys; no button copies, cuts or deletes tiles. Tile Properties is `Tab::TileProperties`, a tab that floats in both modes (`Tab::floats`, tabs.rs:128), drawn by `tile_select::ui` (tile_select.rs:1030-1318) with OK (tile_select.rs:1107) and Cancel and a question when closed with changes (`closing_window`, tile_select.rs:1324); its variants are drawn by `variant_picture` (tile_select.rs:1731), not the shared picture tile.
- The handles are painted in `overlays` (area_view.rs:4584-5084): spawn points (:4646-4690), rings (:4751), selection boxes (:4776-4800), the turning ring (:4839), the scale handle (:4848-4890), tilt rings (:4892), the arrows (about :4923-4960), the start location (:5022); their geometry and hit tests are `turn_rings` (:1763), `tilt_rings` (:1835), `scale_handles` (:1860). Options' "Show the turning and tilt rings…" is `no_turn_ring` (options.rs:936, read at area_view.rs:3495).
- A placed object's Properties: a double click (area_view.rs:5553-5559) or the context menu calls `open_properties` (:6637), which opens `Tab::Instance` (tabs.rs:71), drawn by `blueprint::edit_many` (blueprint/mod.rs:2007): OK and Cancel first (:2050), then the pages as a wrapped row of selectables (:2062-2066; `instance_pages`, :1994).
- The palette is `palette_view::ui` (palette_view.rs:1109-1946): the types' strip (:1214-1244; a dropdown under 300 points, `TYPE_COMBO_UNDER`, :1039), Standard and Custom (:1324-1336), the search, the fold row (Expand All, Collapse All, List, Gallery, New…, More, :1420-1466), Group by (:1535-1544), the gallery's slider (`appearance_gallery::size_slider`, appearance_gallery.rs:202, called at palette_view.rs:1508).
- Docks: `editor_brings_outliner` (shell.rs:264) and `editor_brings_palette` (:274), read by `Panel::available` (:231); the Right Dock (`right_dock`, :1778) draws Palette and Preview as one tab bar, or in the wide layout as two columns with the Preview in the second (:1871-1910). Status Bar: `area_view/bar.rs` (`status`, :25, the states' hints, the counts, `selection_counts`).
- Tests: `common::area_tool` (common.rs:644, a button inside "Area toolbar") is used 58 times (area_view 19, tiles 13, areas 7, drawing 6, outliner, tree and options_and_keys 3 each), and about 110 lines name a toolbar label; `in_toolbar` (:616) and `apart` (:631) leave the group out; 25 lines set `toolbar_icons_only`, `hidden_area_tools` or `hidden_in_areas` (icon_tips.rs, options_and_keys.rs:783-926, areas.rs:400). Pictures: `area_toolbar_narrow` (screens.rs:5245), `toolbar_icons_only` (:5297), the `area_*` and `tile_*` cases, the `shell_*` family. `frame_perf` opens areas by action and clicks by label (frame_perf.rs:620, :629).

**Blueprints, Module Properties and Area Properties.**

- Each kind has a `PAGES` constant (creature.rs:23, 14 pages; item 7, placeable 10, door 10, trigger 8, encounter 6, sound 5, store 6, waypoint 5), `pages()` (blueprint/mod.rs:51) chooses by type, a page is drawn by its name, and the chosen page is `app.blueprint_pages` (:68). Module Properties has an enum (`module_props::Page`, module_props.rs:35, six pages; a plain row, :104-108; OK and Cancel, :85); Area Properties a constant (area_props.rs:19, eight; six shared when several are edited, :29; the row :132-136; OK and Cancel :44).
- The Preview panel shows the palette's blueprint (`area_tools::preview_body`, area_tools.rs:818), never the open blueprint's. #### Part 2. Architecture decisions for M4

1. **The kit's new parts (`mg-uikit`, add-only, egui alone).** Each lands with its first user, as M1 had it ("helpers come with the milestones that first use them"), and none names a type of `mg-ui`, so that the viewer can take it at M6.
   - `header.rs` (U1): `EditorHeader`, 30 points: a left group (what you do), a spacer, a right group (how the view looks), an end slot (OK and Cancel, or Close). It lays itself out against the width it has (section 6.1): first the left group's word buttons lose their words, then they move into a **More** popover, secondary commands before Save; the end slot never yields and is never covered. It records where each control went (on the row, as an icon, in More), so that every editor's test can narrow it to its least width and find each control.
   - `popover.rs` (U1): `Popover`, hung below or below-right of its button (never over the view's top-right overlays), radius 4, `--shadow`; a title with an optional master switch, sub headings, check rows, separators; `Popover::unfolded` lays the same rows into the header as toggles where the row has room (section 5.3).
   - `shelf.rs` (U1): `ToolShelf`, 36 points, 28-point buttons, on, hover, disabled, separators, one accessible group named "Tools".
   - The view's overlays (U4): the compass painter (the light board's `cp-*` tokens) and the view's corner buttons; the readout chip (U8; theme-aware, section 11.5).
   - `pages.rs` (U6 and U9): `PageRail` (a panel's pages as icons at its left edge, the Properties panel's) and `PageList` (a form's pages at its left, with icons, marking the pages in view) with `PageBar` (the bar over each page on the one scroll).
   - `form.rs` (U10): columns of 440 to 520 points for forms.
   - `dialog.rs` (U26 and U27): `Footer` (46 points, a rule above, a setting or count at the left, buttons at the right, the main one first in `accent-fill`), the body's 12 points, `StepList` (a check on done steps) and the wizard's page-header bar; `EmptyState` (U24).
   - `gallery.rs` (U25): `GalleryCell` (Quiet Tiles, section 8.4: rim, name rule, detail line, states, the kind's icon while making, "No model" badge, favorite mark, the small variant), `GalleryGrid` (cells that grow, and fixed cells in justified rows) and the one size slider, 64 to 220 (`appearance_gallery.rs:198-199` already clamps to it).
   - Three known differences of M2 are the kit's to settle where its parts draw them: the open combo box in `raised-hover` (U3), a disabled kit control drawn in its own tokens rather than faded whole (U1), the slider's thumb in `text-2` (U25).
2. **The docks hold what the active editor brings.** M3's registry is generalized in U2, before any editor needs it:
   - `Dock` gains `Bottom`. A dock holds **sections** (up to three stacked in the Right Dock, as the Talk, Factions and NUI boards draw them), each a tab bar of one or more panels. The Main board's Right Dock is two sections (Palette and Preview; Properties), the Conversation board's two (Node, Data, Search; Conversation), the Script board's two (Reference; Help).
   - `editor_brings(app)` replaces `editor_brings_palette` and `editor_brings_outliner`: by the active docked editor's kind it gives the Left Dock's Outliner contents, the Right Dock's sections and the Bottom Dock's own panels (a script's Compiler and Bookmarks, the NUI designer's Checks). The global panels (Log, Problems, Search Results) stay whatever the editor.
   - Under 1400 points the sections fold into one tab bar (section 5.2; Narrow draws Palette, Properties, Preview), in the wide layout the first section takes the first column and the rest the second (WideArea: Palette and Preview, then Properties; the Preview goes back to the first column, as T14 left it to do).
   - A panel's body is one function taking the editor's tab; the dock calls it when the editor is docked and in front, the editor's own pane when it floats. A body that draws a 3D view the editor may also draw uses the late slot, generalized from `preview_slot`.
   - Which tab of a section is in front and the sections' shares are kept per editor kind in `Settings` (as `right_dock_width` is), not per document.
   - The Bottom Dock gets N tabs and the Status Bar N switches, each with its count badge (Problems' errors, Search Results' hits, Checks'), icons alone under 1400 (`Yields::status_switch_icons`), the switches' width arithmetic (shell.rs:916-930) made general.
   - A panel exists only once its feeder is built: **no merge point shows a panel nothing can fill** (M3's rule kept). From then on Problems and Search Results show their switches as every board draws them, with no module open too (Welcome.png), their body an empty state saying what fills it.
   - The Plugins menu's "pane last clicked" (`plugins.pane`) stays as T13 left it, no Outliner counting; a panel an editor brings counts as that editor's pane (decided in U2 and written into 17-plugin-api.md).
   - Why now: the boards draw every editor this way, and doing it once keeps each editor's task to its own panels.
3. **Each editor's Outliner** (S5): the Left Dock's Outliner shows, by the active editor, an area's objects (T13), a conversation's Bookmarks (U15), a 2DA's columns with their eyes (U16), the NUI window's layers (U18), a tileset's parts (U20), a hak's contents by type (U21), the factions (U22). One `outliner::contents` chooses; the kit's `TreeGroup::eye` and `TreeRow::second` draw them.
4. **OK and Cancel move into the header's end slot** by one change to `ok_cancel_saying` (an `in_header` form, the same tips and `Pressed`), taken up by each editor's own task, so that the 13 callers move one at a time; Options' own pair (options.rs:701-727) the same in U23. Escape (R1) keeps reading where the buttons are drawn (`cancel_rects`). GitHub issue 38's fix holds with them: a tab that pins its buttons and scrolls its own page fits its pane (`TabViewer::scroll_bars` gives `[false, false]`), and `a_properties_window_s_buttons_stay_put` runs at 1.0, 1.25 and 1.5 for every editor moved (the agdb note "Windows with OK and Cancel at their foot fit their pane").
5. **The dialogs that become panels** (ruling 5): Find Instance and the module-wide Find and Replace Text's hits go to Search Results, the search's form as the panel's header; Build Module's results to Problems (Q4; Verify's findings, Q5); Hak Pak Conflict Analysis, Resources Used and Claims Table become Bottom Dock tabs opened by their commands; Edit Areas Together, Light Maker and Bake Walkmesh become sections of the area editor's Right Dock while open; Plugins becomes a tab. Their `Moonglow` fields (`find_instance`, lib.rs:915; `text_replace`, :1026; `build`, :919; `hak_report`, :1057; `area_stats`, :929; `claims.table`; `area_chooser`, :1024; `light_draft`, :908; `bake.draft`, :911; `plugins.window`, :1341) become the panels' state, and their commands show the panel. Areas Not Yours is a question asked when saving (claims.rs:851), so it stays a dialog with the confirmations.
6. **Settings and their migrations.** `Settings::default()` keeps its meaning; nothing becomes As Tabs for an existing builder.
   - `toolbar_icons_only` is retired in U23 (R4): the field, its draft and the Options control go; an old file still reads, the value dropped silently, nothing unread and no copy put aside (the precedent test at settings.rs:2000-2017); an older Moonglow reading a newer file takes its default, Icons and text, which only its own toolbars read. `icons::Tools` keeps its Top Bar use (`icons_alone`) and loses the rest.
   - `hidden_area_tools` (settings.rs:820) stays, with its 29 names: a name hides the control from the header row, from its popover and from the wide layout's unfolded row; the header's right-click menu and Options › Area edit it (the moves row "The strip's right-click menu (which buttons to show)"). Names are kept so stored lists keep their meaning.
   - New: the docks' per-kind sections (above). Retired, read silently: `talk_splits` with the talk table's splitter (U17).
   - Tile Properties stops being a floating tab (`Tab::floats`); an open-tabs record naming it shows the panel instead.
7. **Moonglow Viewer** is not affected by any M4 change (it takes neither crate). The kit's crate comment says the viewer uses it, which is true only from M6; U30 says so.
8. **For the owner:** Q1 to Q5 below. The rest is decided by the boards, the proposal or an existing ruling:
   - The Properties panel and Open in Tab: the Main and Floating boards draw the panel in both modes; Open in Tab opens today's tab (or window) with OK and Cancel.
   - The Terrain button of the tool shelf ("Paint terrain with the tile palette's brushes", the boards' tip): it shows the Palette on its Tiles type and is on while a terrain brush is in hand; choosing a terrain brush turns it on.
   - The area toolbar's "problems" and "N missing" (no board draws them; nothing disappears): a warning icon with its count at the right group's end, before More, its tip saying what was read.
   - Search Results is one panel (every board draws one switch), showing the last search, its form as its header.
   - Finding 13.2 is fixed in U14 (the Node panel shows that line; the board drew today's words) and finding 13.3 in U24 (the recent row is rebuilt).



#### Part 3. The plan for M4

Each task names what it builds (board by board), the moves rows it ticks (by their text), the known differences it settles, its Status Bar hints and counts (through `shell::shown`, keys by `HintKeys`), its tests (each new test seen to fail without the change), its pictures, its timing, its docs and the deferred entries it closes or must keep (by heading and line of `docs/deferred.md` today). Manual chapters by file; parity sections of `docs/parity/checklists.md` by heading. "Docked and floating" means a test in each mode (`common::Mode`).

##### M4a: The area editor and the handles (U0 to U8)

**U0. The editors' pictures and the baseline (do first; 1 day).**

No `src/` change.

- **Coherent.** Yes.

**Done, 2026-11-14.** The 27 cases are in `screens.rs`, each `#[ignore]` and named as the list above names them; run them with `cargo test -p mg-ui --test screens -- --ignored board_ --test-threads=1` (pictures go to `screens/board/`, or to `screens-light/board/` with `MG_LIGHT=1`). They write 37 pictures, because the sheets get one picture per state: `board_gizmo_states_selected`, `_shift` and `_drag`; `board_dialogs_rename`, `_delete`, `_find_replace`, `_build`, `_area_wizard` and `_creature_wizard`; `board_pickers_portrait`, `_texture`, `_armor` and `_creature_wizard`. The sheets' windows are 1600 by 720; the rest use the board's size.

`shell_main` stays as M3 left it, with editors floating. `board_main` is the Main board As Tabs and is not an alias of it. The shared set-up is `board_window`, built on `shell_with_area`: As Tabs; the boards' tabs (Module Properties, the area with its modified dot, Faribeth, the script); the Plague Victim Pyre selected under the boards' camera (`BOARD_CAMERA`); the Right Dock on Placeables; the log closed. `area_changed`, `pyre_index` and `resources_chicken` now serve `board_tabs`, `shell_outliner` and `shell_resources_window` too. No `src/` change.

Each case's comment says what today's app shows in place of its board. The pictures are in `target/ui-mock/impl/m4-u0/` (`dark/`, `light/`), and `INDEX.md` there lists one line of differences per case.

What today's app cannot show, with the nearest state each case uses instead:
