The Appearance and Placeable Galleries already open as tabs As Tabs.

**The baseline.** Release binaries were built once (`--no-run`). Each test then ran alone (`--ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1`) from `crates/mg-ui`, through `perf-m4/u0/run.sh`, which waits before each run for a 1-minute load under 3. The set ran twice: `frame_perf`, `frame_perf` at `FRAME_SCREEN=1280x800`, `editor_perf` and `nui_perf`, then the same again with logs prefixed `run2_`. Loads at the starts were 2.89, 2.93, 2.46 and 2.42 for the first set, and 2.21, 2.34, 2.83 and 2.92 for the second (`loads.txt`).

This tree's code is T15's, so a view counts as moved only where both runs differ from T15's quiet logs by more than 0.3 ms in the same direction (`agree.py`; against T15's interleaved `ab2` logs, `agree_ab2.txt`). The median view moved -0.020 and +0.010 ms (339 views), -0.010 and +0.040 ms at 1280 by 800 (327), and +0.08 and +0.17 ms in `editor_perf` (19).

In the first run, area092's stretch of `frame_perf` ran at about three times its time, tessellation included, so the processor was taken. That run failed its budget check (tiles palette searched as typed, wheel, 14.08 ms; all selected with the walkmesh, 11.5 to 12.3 ms). The second run did not repeat it (3.05 to 3.74 ms) and passed every test, so `run2_frame_perf.log` is the baseline.

Views moved beyond 0.3 ms in both runs, T15 then run 1 then run 2, in ms:

- **area092, wheel, at the default size.** The overview went 2.71, 7.05, 3.05; the tiles palette searched as typed 3.06, 14.08, 3.74; all selected with the walkmesh 3.13, 12.29, 3.53. Only the second run's 0.3 to 0.7 ms is in the comparison.
- **T15's own spikes, which its note names, against T15's single quiet run.** Area Properties went 3.30, 3.13 and 2.65 to about 1.63. area084's one-column Palette in front went 8.80 to 2.25 and 2.32 (idle) and 9.96 to 4.85 and 5.22 (wheel).
- **Slower, at the default size.** area084's Outliner kinds closed (wheel) went 3.73 to 4.34 in both runs.
- **Quicker, at the default size.** The resource browser (wheel) went 0.86 to 0.50. The lake with Shaders off, turning (pointer), went 2.90 to 2.17 and 2.53. Several area084 wheel views were 0.3 to 1.0 ms quicker: turning, two columns, all selected with the walkmesh.
- **At 1280 by 800, the lake's wheel and walkmesh views were 0.3 to 2.0 ms slower.** With Shaders on, all selected with the walkmesh (pointer), went 3.48 to 4.24 and 5.51.
- **`editor_perf`.** The first frame went 262.0 to 266.2 and 265.6. The frame the check as you type compiles in went 7.76 to 8.17 and 8.32.

The tree's code is unchanged, so these moves are the shared machine's.

Over the 6.94 ms budget in both runs:

- area084's overview and turning views (wheel), with Sound Ranges on and off, at 7.7 to 10.9 ms at both sizes, as at T15.
- area092's edit frame: 7.7 ms in the second run, 7.1 at T15.
- area084's edit frames: 11.1 and 12.0 ms, as at T15.

area092's overview and turning views are under budget in the second run (0.9 to 3.1 ms at the default size, up to 4.3 ms at 1280 by 800), as at T15. Nothing is newly over budget.

`nui_perf` has no T15 log, so its figures are a baseline only, first run and second run:

- a large window's idle frame: 1.00 and 0.99 ms;
- a frame after an edit of the window: 1.96 and 2.06 ms;
- a frame after an edit elsewhere: 1.00 and 1.00 ms;
- a window of text, idle: 0.74 and 0.73 ms;
- a chart of a million samples, idle: 29.8 and 38.4 ms, the one view over budget.

**U1. The kit's header, popover and tool shelf (2 days).**

- **Builds.** `EditorHeader`, `Popover`, More, `ToolShelf` (Part 2, decision 1), measured from `moonglow.css` (`.editor-header`, `.popover` with `.pop-title`, `.pop-h`, `.pop-row` and `.pop-sep`, `.shelf`); a disabled kit button in `text-off` and its tokens (known difference "a disabled control fades whole", for the kit's controls). A test helper `common::header_holds(h, group, names)`: each name on the row, as an icon, or in More.
- **User sees.** Nothing.
- **Hands on.** The header, popover and shelf to U3 and every editor after; `header_holds` to each editor's narrowing test.
- **Tests.** Kit: the yields in order (words, icons, More; the end slot never), at widths from the header's full width down to its end slot; a popover below-right never over the top-right corner; a master switch's state; the kit sheet against Foundations and LightFoundations.
- **Coherent.** Yes.

**Done, 2026-11-14.** Four new modules in `mg-uikit`, egui alone, none naming an `mg-ui` type; nothing in the application uses them yet, so nothing changes for the user.

- **`button`: `KitButton` and `ButtonLook`** (Raised `.btn`, Flat `.btn-icon` and `.btn.flat`, Toggle, Primary): an icon, words or both, a chevron where it opens something (`opens`), the open look (`raised-hover` and an `accent` ring; `open_state` without a chevron, More's `⋯`), measured before it is laid out (`width`, the same in every state). Disabled, it is drawn in the disabled tokens, not faded: `text-off` on `raised` (on nothing where flat), a toggle that is on in `accent-fill-off` and `on-fill-off` (a primary as a word button, `raised` and `text-off`: corrected in the review below, C2). Inside a disabled `Ui` the fade is taken back out and a parent's opacity kept (`controls::box_painter`, now `pub(crate)`). This settles "A disabled control fades whole" for the kit's new parts. `IconButton` and egui's own buttons still fade: changing them would change every existing toolbar now, so each editor's header settles it as it moves onto `KitButton` (U3 on).
- **`header`: `EditorHeader`, `Item`, `Place`, `Yield`, `HeaderOutput`, `places`, `more_name`.** The row is 30 px of `bar` with a `line` under it, padding 6 and gap 4: a left group, a spacer, a right group, More, a line, and the end slot (`show_with_end(ui, width, closure)`, the width the caller's, as `three_parts_sized` takes it; the closure's value comes back in `end`). Items: `button`, `words`, `icon`, `toggle(icon, words, &mut bool)`, `popover(icon, Popover)`, `menu(icon, words, closure)`, `custom(name, width, closure)` (fields, combo boxes, segmented controls, notes; `more(width, closure)` gives it a form in More) and `separator`. Modifiers: `in_more` (always in More), `yields`, `unfolds`, `icon_only` (also for a popover's or menu's button: the compact header's icon and chevron), `enabled`, `tip`, `look`, `words_icon`. Header settings: `more_words` ("More ▾" rather than `⋯`), `more_after(name)`, `end_separator`. Everything is measured in the same frame, so a width always gives the same row, both ways. The yields are taken one step at a time: an unfolded popover folds (from the right group's end), the left group's words go from its end to its start, then the right group's, then items move into More in the same order (the items marked `primary`, Save, last of all: corrected in the review below, B3). The end slot keeps the right end at every width. Where even More does not fit beside it, More and what is in it are cut, as is any item that may not yield and reaches More or the end slot. Cut items are not drawn and are recorded as `Place::Cut`. More holds, in the row's order, buttons as rows, toggles as check rows, a popover's rows under a heading (its switch a check row), a menu's rows under a heading, and a custom item's More form. A line at the right group's end stays where More follows it (the Script board's codepage, a line, `⋯`). The row takes no stop of Tab, so Tab goes from item to item; a right click anywhere on it, over its items too, opens `HeaderOutput::context_menu` (corrected in the review below, B1). It records each item's `Place`, and an unfolded popover's switch and rows, in its output and per header (`header::records`, `places` the first; corrected in the review below, B4). One popover of a header is open at a time. Its rectangle is `HeaderOutput::popover_rect`.
- **`popover`: `Popover`, `PopCheck`, `PopAction`, `Hang`, `PopoverOutput`, `paint_switch`.** It is described once and shown three ways: `show(ui, &button)` (open state kept under the button's id), `show_hung(ctx, id, anchor, frame, &mut open)` (the header's), `show_in_place` (a catalog's) and `show_unfolded` (measured first by `unfolded_width`). Its parts are a title (`.pop-title`, 28 px, a line, 4 under it) with an optional master switch (26 by 14), whose rows are said disabled while it is off and keep their values (`rows_follow_switch`). Then sub headings and separators (the kit's `menu_heading` and `menu_separator`), check rows (box, optional icon, words; `sub` 32 px in; lit `hover-row`), action rows (icon, words, a weak note at the right end; chosen, they close the popover and are named in `clicked`), and rows of the caller's (`custom`, or `custom_unfolded` with a form for the row). It is at least 220 wide, `panel` with a `line-soft` border, radius 4 and `--shadow`, 4 px under its button. `Hang::BelowRight` aligns right edges, so the popover never reaches right of its button; `Hang::Auto` resolves by the button's side of the header's middle. **It is the kit's own `Area`, not an egui popup**, because egui keeps one popup open at a time: a combo box's list opened from a row would close it (the NUI designer's known difference). It closes on a click outside it and its button, or on Escape, except while an egui popup is open over it (checked as the frame begins). It is kept inside the window: moved, never flipped to the other side of its button. Since egui's popup memory does not see it, `Popover::any_open(ctx)` says whether one was open this pass or the last. U3 adds it to what Escape's rule (`widgets::dialogs`' `escape`) and `shell::keys_blocked` ask, beside `egui::Popup::is_any_open`, so that an Escape closing a popover (or `header_holds` closing More) cancels no docked editor. Unfolded, a check row is a toggle (its icon, or its words with `unfolded_words`), an action a word button, a separator a line, and the master switch a toggle with the title's icon. A popover with a row lacking an unfolded form does not unfold (`can_unfold`).
- **`shelf`: `ToolShelf`, `Tool`, `ShelfOutput`, `TOOLS`.** A 36 px strip of `bar` with a `line` at its right, padding 4 and gap 2. Tools are 28 px, frameless in `text-2`, `raised` hovered, `accent-fill` on, and `text-off` disabled (not faded). Separators are 20 by 1 of `line-soft`. It is one group named "Tools", each tool said on or not, its tip its name where none is given.
- **`shell::VSEP_WIDTH`** (9) names the width `vsep` already had.

Tests (each seen to fail once with its behavior broken; the breaks and their failures are in the task's report; the review below found two orders the yields test did not hold, G1 and G9, which it holds since). The kit's `tests/kit/header.rs`: `the_header_yields_words_then_icons_then_more` narrows a script-like header in 10 px steps from 1400 to its end slot's width and widens it again. It asserts the end slot's place and width, nothing past the row or over the end slot, monotone forms, the order (the left group's words from its end, nothing into More while a word keeps its words), the same row both ways, and every name found once on the row or in More. Further tests: `more_holds_buttons_and_toggles`, `a_popover_hangs_below_right_never_over_the_top_right_corner`, `a_master_switch_turns_its_rows_off_and_back`, `a_combo_inside_a_popover_leaves_it_open`, `an_action_row_closes_its_popover`, `a_popover_button_can_be_kept_to_its_icon`, `tab_goes_from_item_to_item`, `a_menu_opens_from_its_button_and_a_row_closes_it`, `more_holds_menus_parts_and_popovers` (a menu's rows, a custom item's More form, a popover's switch and rows, More kept inside a narrow window), `more_stands_where_it_is_asked` (`more_after`, `more_words`), `a_line_stands_before_more`, `an_open_popover_is_seen_open`, `the_tool_shelf_reports_its_tools`, `a_disabled_kit_button_is_not_faded` (its text unfaded in `text-off`, its fill `raised`, in both themes) and `auto_hangs_by_the_side_of_the_middle`; and `button.rs`'s two unit tests of the looks' tokens. The kit sheet gains a cell of the header at four widths (unfolded, as given, words gone, things in More), the kit button's states, the Lighting and a Brush popover in place, and a shelf (`target/ui-mock/impl/m4-u1/`, dark and light, with the sheet before).

`common::header_holds(h, group, names)` (in `crates/mg-ui/tests/app/common.rs`, generic over the harness's state) reads `header::records`. It finds each name on the row within the header's group (for an unfolded popover, one of its rows), drawn inside the row and clear of the end slot and More, or opens More and finds it in `More in <group>`, drawn inside its popover, then closes More with Escape (the rectangles: corrected in the review below, A2; `header_holds_nth` for the second header of a name). A name cut or missing fails, named. `yields::a_header_holds_its_controls_down_to_its_least_width` drives a bare kit header with it from 1200 to its least width.

How the editors write their headers with it, unchanged:

- **U3, the area.** The left group holds the kind toggles as one `joined` group (since the review, C3; All and None on an `icon_only` menu beside it; under E 990, by `Yields::header_compact`, a `popover(Eye, "Show")` of check rows and All and None actions, its words carrying the count), Snap and Turn as `custom` combos (their `compact` form without value text, given under 550 by `Yields::value_text`, or taken where the row narrows: since the review, D4), and Together and Onto Objects as icon toggles (`in_more` under 490, by `Yields::into_more`). The right group holds Day | Night as a `custom` segmented control (compact: one moon toggle), then Lighting, Overlays (`switch(&mut on, "Show overlays")`; Walkmesh's menu folds into its rows) and Audio as `popover(…).unfolds()` (compact: `.icon_only()`; the wide row unfolds them where they fit, Fade Geometry and Shadows by `custom_unfolded`), Area Properties as `button` (compact: `icon_only`) and the warning as a `custom` item. To Scratch and Save as Prefab… are `in_more`. `HeaderOutput::context_menu` is `toolbar_menu`, and a hidden tool is an item left out.
- **U4.** Paint's options take the left group (a `custom` segmented control, `custom` number fields, a Brush `popover` whose combo boxes stay open) and the shelf is `ToolShelf`.
- **U12, the script.** Save and Compile are `button`s; Save As…, Print…, Open… and External Editor `icon`s; Find… and Replace… `custom` (joined) or two `icon`s; Bookmark an icon `toggle`; Definition, References, Rename Symbol… and Used By `icon`s; To Scratch is `in_more`. The codepage is a right `custom` item followed by a `separator`, which stays before More.
- **U14, the conversation** (Conversation_crop_header). Add is a `button`; Copy, Cut, Paste, Paste As Link, Delete, the arrows, Expand All and Collapse All are `icon`s between `separator`s. The right group holds the five highlights as a `joined` group (since the review, C3), Scripts as a `toggle` with its icon and words, Export as a `menu` with `words_icon(true)`, Import Lines… as a `button` and Test as a `button`; OK and Cancel go in the end slot. The header keeps the body's 13 points whatever the editor's own text size (Options › Conversation Editor): it is chrome, as the Top Bar is, and the 30-point row could not hold larger text. Since the review (D9) the header sets the kit's sizes back for its row and popovers itself, so U14 draws it where it likes; today's toolbar, which grows with that setting, does not.
- **U16 on.** The 2DA editor's Add Row count, Find, Go to and "N cells are wrong" are `custom`; Values as names and Strings as text are right icon `toggle`s; it uses `more_words(true)` with its four `in_more` items; its own Undo and Redo go. The talk table's Export is a `menu` with `words_icon(true)`, and Close (read-only) the end slot. The NUI designer's pages are a `custom` segmented control, Build & Compile a `button` with `look(Primary)` and `icon_only()`, More stands after Export… (`more_after`), and View is a `popover` with combo rows. The tileset's pages are a `custom` segmented control. The hak's Remove (3) is `words`, its search a `custom` field (the kit's header replaces `Tools::fitted`). The journal, factions, read-only resource and Options are the same items and the end slot. Every editor's narrowing test ends in `header_holds` at its least width.

Not built here, by the plan: the compass, the view's corner buttons and the readout chip (U4, U8), and the page list, footer and gallery cell (later tasks). Nothing in `mg-ui` draws the new parts yet. No deferred entry is settled or added (230 before and after). The next tasks inherit:

- popover rows have no hovered state to force for a catalog, as the menu's do (`as_hovered`);
- a popover's check rows have no keyboard focus ring of their own beyond the row's fill;
- `Popover::any_open` is not yet asked by the application's Escape rule (U3 wires it, with the first popover the application shows).

**Review, 2026-11-15.** An independent review of U1's change (ca15bfe2) found seven faults, settled seven suspicions, three differences from the boards and seven gaps in the API later tasks need. Each fix has a test, seen to fail with its fix taken out; the failure text is quoted. The new tests are in `crates/mg-uikit/tests/kit/header_fixes.rs` unless named otherwise.

Faults:

- **A1. An item's `enabled(false)` was dropped** in More (a popover's, a menu's, a custom item's form), unfolded, and for a custom item on the row: a disabled popover's Grid row flipped in More. The fix carries `enabled` into each of them. `Popover::enabled` disables the switch and every row, hung, unfolded and in More; a menu's rows in More are drawn in a disabled `Ui`; a custom item's `Ui` is disabled on the row, in its compact form and in More; a joined group's buttons are disabled too. Tests, one per place:
  - `a_disabled_popover_is_disabled_in_more`: "assertion failed: … get_by_label("Grid").accesskit_node().is_disabled()";
  - `a_disabled_menu_is_disabled_in_more`: "… get_by_label("CSV…") … is_disabled()";
  - `a_disabled_custom_item_is_disabled_everywhere`: "row enabled: [("row", true)]" with the row's fix out; "the More form enabled: [("more", false), ("more", true), …]" with the More form's;
  - `a_disabled_popover_is_disabled_unfolded`: "an unfolded row of a disabled popover";
  - `a_disabled_joined_group_is_disabled`: "assertion failed: node.accesskit_node().is_disabled()".
- **A2. `header_holds` proved only that a node existed.** The header now records the row's, the end slot's, More's and an open popover's rectangles (`header::records`). `header_holds` checks each control lies inside the row and clear of the end slot and More, or inside More's popover. With the row's items drawn 5000 to the right, `yields::a_header_holds_its_controls_down_to_its_least_width` fails: "Save is drawn outside Kit header's row: [[5014.0 11.5] - [5077.0 33.5]] in [[8.0 8.0] - [1192.0 38.0]]".
- **A3, and B9 with it. More kept its old width after its own button closed it.** The popover's "shown" flag was cleared only by `show_hung`, which is not called on that close. Every close path, a popover giving way to another, and a header that missed a pass now call `Popover::forget` (public, as is `Popover::focus_in`). `more_is_measured_again_after_any_close` failed: "More kept its width: 332 after 332".
- **A4. A header popover reopened by itself** when its header came back after a pass not drawn (another tab in front). The open item is kept with the pass it was drawn in and dropped when the header missed one. `a_popover_does_not_reopen_by_itself` failed: "the popover came back by itself".
- **A5. `controls::box_painter` divided the fade out in an enabled `Ui`** too, lifting a parent's opacity (a fading window's) to full for a `KitButton` disabled by itself. It now divides only where egui faded, in a disabled `Ui`. **This changes existing kit code (the add-only rule):** its other callers (check box, radio, segmented control, a menu's check and radio rows) pass `ui.is_enabled()`, or the response's enabled state, which egui takes from the `Ui`. Where they pass false the `Ui` is disabled, so they look as before. `a_disabled_kit_button_keeps_its_parent_s_opacity` failed: "Save: #5F_66_72_FF" (alpha FF under a parent's 0.5); the extended unit test `controls::tests::a_disabled_box_keeps_a_parent_s_opacity` failed: "1".
- **A6. Tab did not go into an open popover.** A popover opened by the keyboard (a click with no pointer click: Enter or Space) now takes the focus to its first row that takes it (the switch, a check or an action row), and Tab goes on through its rows. This covers the header's popovers and `Popover::show`. `the_keyboard_goes_into_a_popover_it_opened` failed: "the focus stayed outside".
- **A7. Under the end slot's width the end slot was drawn outside the row** (a 60 px window: from −74 to 46). Every part's `Ui` is now clipped to the row. The least width is documented in `header`'s comment: the end slot's and the padding, `end_width + 12`. `the_end_slot_stays_inside_a_row_too_narrow` failed: "drawn outside the row: [[0.0 0.0] - [60.0 100.0]]".

Suspicions, each settled:

- **B1, a fault. A right click on an item never reached the row**, only one on a gap. `HeaderOutput::secondary_clicked` is now true for a right click anywhere on the row, and `HeaderOutput::context_menu(add)` opens the header's own menu at the pointer in the kit's menu style. `HeaderOutput::responses` and `response(name)` give each item's response (D1). `a_right_click_anywhere_on_the_row_reaches_it` failed with the row's own `secondary_clicked()` as the condition: "assertion `left == right` failed: a right click on Save and on a gap".
- **B2, a fault. A menu closed on any click in its rows' rectangle**, headings and disabled rows included. It now closes only where the widget egui reports clicked is an enabled widget inside the rows that senses a click and not a drag (a button). The popover's own `Area` and a selectable label, whose text a drag selects, are reported clicked too and are left out. `a_menu_closes_on_an_enabled_row_only` failed: "closed by a heading or a disabled row".
- **B3, the owner's ruling. Save moves into More last.** `Item::primary()` marks a header's first commands (one or more); they move into More after everything else that may, the right group's items included. Otherwise the left group goes from its end, as before. Their words go at the left group's step, as others' do. The order is tested in two places:
  - `the_first_command_goes_into_more_last`: "Save into More before Day at 350";
  - the yields test, now with Save marked: "Save into More before Day at 370".

  Guard G1, More filled from the left group's start, now fails the yields test: "Compile into More before Open… at 550" (all sixteen header tests had passed with it).
- **B4, a fault. Two headers of one name shared one record.** Records are kept per header id, `header::records(ctx, name)` gives each header's in the order their rows stand (`HeaderRecord`), and `places` gives the first's. `common::header_holds_nth` takes which header; `yields::two_headers_of_one_name_are_each_held` drives two. `two_headers_of_one_name_keep_a_record_each` failed with one record per name: "assertion `left == right` failed".
- **B5, a fault. A tall popover had no scroll** and climbed over its button in a short window. A hung popover is now no taller than the room under its button (or over it, hung above); what does not fit scrolls. `a_tall_popover_scrolls_under_its_button` failed: "over its button: [[14.0 0.0] - [244.0 260.0]]".
- **B6, a fault. The shelf clipped its tools silently.** Where it is too short, the tools that do not fit go into a **More Tools** tool at its foot (`more-vertical`, on while a tool in it is on), whose popover, hung above it (`Hang::Above`, D7), lists them; one chosen there is reported clicked by its index, as on the shelf. `a_short_shelf_puts_its_last_tools_in_more` failed: "No nodes found matching the query" (no More Tools).
- **B7. The master switch's role.** accesskit 0.24 has `Role::Switch`, which egui's widget types do not offer. The switch now replaces its node's role, keeping its name and toggled state. `the_master_switch_is_a_switch` failed: "assertion `left == right` failed" (`CheckBox`). A disabled popover's switch is drawn in the disabled tokens.
- **B8, a fault. An action row drawn in place called `ui.close()`**, which closed a closable parent of the catalog's. `show_in_place` now gives the body a closable scope of its own. `an_action_in_place_closes_no_parent` failed: "the catalog's parent was asked to close".
- **B9** is A3's.

The boards:

- **C1.** A word button's icon alone (the left group's words gone), and a popover's or menu's compact icon and chevron, are now framed (`raised`, the icon in `text`), as Narrow.png draws Lighting, Overlays, Audio and Area Properties. `ButtonLook::Flat` stays `.btn-icon` (`Item::icon`, More's `⋯`). `button::tests` failed with the old rule: "assertion `left == right` failed".

It yields as one, straight into More, where it is a heading of its name over a check row per toggle and a row per button. Its buttons are recorded in its place. `a_joined_group_yields_as_one` failed with a 4 px gap: "a 1 px seam: [[14.0 11.5] - [36.0 33.5]] [[40.0 11.5] - [62.0 33.5]]".

Documents:

**U2. The docks hold what an editor brings (2 days).**

- **Builds.** Part 2, decision 2: `Dock::Bottom`, sections, `editor_brings`, panel bodies with two hosts, the late slot, per-kind layouts in `Settings`, N Bottom Dock tabs and N Status Bar switches with badges. The area's Palette and Preview move onto it unchanged.
- **User sees.** Nothing (the Right Dock as today; the Log alone below).
- **Tests.** Unit: sections folded into one bar under 1400 and split into columns in the wide layout; the switches' widths for one to five switches, as `status_bar.rs`'s sweep does for one. App: every `right_dock.rs` and `status_bar.rs` test unchanged; a dock with no available panel is not drawn.
- **Timing.** `frame_perf` (the docks are drawn every frame).
- **Hands on.** Sections, `editor_brings` and the Bottom Dock's tabs to U5 and U6 (the area), U11 to U13 (blueprints, script) and every editor after.
- **Coherent.** Yes.

**Done, 2026-11-15.** **Built** (all in `crates/mg-ui/src/shell.rs` unless named). `Panel` gains `Log`, the Bottom Dock's global panel, and `Dock` gains `Bottom`. What an editor brings is `Brings` (the Outliner; `right`, the Right Dock's sections from the top, each a static slice of panels; `folded`, their order in one bar under 1400; `bottom`, the editor's own Bottom Dock panels; `floats`, whether they follow the editor into its window), given by `brings_of(app, tab)` by the tab's kind and `editor_brings(app)` for the active docked editor; it replaces `editor_brings_palette` and `editor_brings_outliner`, and `Panel::available` reads it (`available_with` for a floating editor's). The area brings the Outliner and one section, Palette and Preview (with the game's data and a module), the placeholder the section alone. `right_sections`, `panels` (the Right Dock's in the folded order, the Bottom Dock's own then `Panel::BOTTOM_TABS`), `switches` (`SWITCHES_BEFORE`, the editor's own, `SWITCHES_AFTER`) and `arrange` (sections, folded order, narrow, columns in; columns of stacked tab bars out) are plain functions. `right_dock` draws one bar exactly as before (same ids, names, nesting), or stacked sections each with its own bar over its share (`section_rects`, `section_heights`; the seams, `section_seams`, made after the sections' widgets so that they are over them, keep the shares per kind when dragged), or the wide layout's two columns (first section, then the rest; a lone section of two stands as its first panel and the rest, today's Palette | Preview, so the user sees nothing until U6 adds a second section). A section's front is the dock's panel chosen last where it holds it, else the run's last choice among its panels (`Moonglow::right_fronts`), else the settings' for the kind, else its first (`section_front`, `choose_right`); fronts and shares are kept by the section's place among the kind's own sections (`own_index`), never for a section it does not bring (the palettes asked for by name beside a script write nothing for the script). `panel_body(app, ui, panel, Host, pane)` is a panel's one body, its host the dock or the editor's window (`window_panes`, called from `TabViewer::ui` for a tab in a window whose kind `floats`: the sections stacked in a right pane by the kind's shares, with the same seams, the own Bottom Dock panels on a bottom pane's tabs, before the editor draws in what is left). The late slot is `LateSlot` (panel, rect, layer, pane) in `Moonglow::late_slots`, drawn by `draw_late` after the editor area (the Preview's by `area_tools::preview_late`, the old `preview_panel`). `bottom_dock` has a tab per panel it holds, the panel in front's tools (`Panel::header_tools`: the Log's Copy, Save… and Clear; the tools' width the widest of the panels', so the tabs keep their form), the front from `bottom_shown` (chosen in the run, else the kind's kept, else the first: the Log today); `status_bar` has a `StatusSwitch` per panel with its `Panel::badge(app)`, on while the dock shows that panel, a click on an off switch opening the dock on it and on an on switch closing it; the icons-alone arithmetic is `switches_width` (each switch's width and `status::GAP` between them), the Log's one switch giving the old sum. `Settings::dock_layouts` (kind name to `DockLayout { fronts, shares, bottom }`, by panel names) is written only once something is chosen (`skip_serializing_if`, so files stay as they were), read where kinds or panels are a newer version's (passed by), and cleared by Reset Layout; an older Moonglow ignores the field (serde's default), tested. F6 (`step_pane`), the keys leaving undrawn panels and `show_dock_panel` go by the bars drawn (`Moonglow::right_bars`) and the Bottom Dock's front instead of the Palette and Preview by name; `palettes_asked` is set only for those two. **Decided**: (1) **The area's front tab was not kept in the settings** (superseded: the owner ruled on 2026-11-15 that the area remembers its tab too; see the Review paragraph): decision 2 keeps fronts per kind in `Settings`, but M3's `the_palette_is_in_front_as_a_module_opens` kept the Right Dock's tab for the run and put the Palette in front as a module opened, so `keeps_fronts` exempted the area and the placeholder. (2) **Orders are data**: the folded order, the Bottom Dock's tab order and the switches' order each come from tables (the Script board's tabs are Compiler, Bookmarks, Search Results, Log and its switches Log, Problems, Compiler, Bookmarks, Search Results, which no single order gives). (3) **The plugins' pane** (decision 2's last but one point, written into 17-plugin-api.md): a press in a panel an editor brings makes that editor's pane the pane last clicked in: the Palette and the Preview the palette, as before; an area's other panels the area; an editor with no pane of its own leaves it as it was. (4) **Test panels**: the generalization is proved in the library's own tests (`shell::dock_tests`, kittest in `src` as `options.rs` has it) with `Panel::Sample(n)` and `Moonglow::sample_brings`, both `#[cfg(test)]`: built into neither the application nor `tests/app` nor `screens.rs`, so nothing fake ships. **Pictures**: `shell_main`, `shell_wide`, every `shell_width_*` (1600 among them), `shell_760`, `board_main`, `board_narrow`, `board_wide`, `board_floating`, Dark and Light, before (the tip `52d640be`) and after: all 44 the same to the pixel (`target/ui-mock/impl/m4-u2/`). **Timing**: `frame_perf` release, each run alone, at 1-minute loads of 2.7 to 3.0 at their starts; the machine shared, so the tip (`52d640be`, built apart from a `git archive` copy) and U2's tree were run interleaved, tip, U2, U2, tip (`target/ui-mock/perf-m4/u2/`, `agree.txt`): of 339 views the median difference is +0.015 ms in each U2 run (median view 1.91 against 1.93 and 2.00 ms; tessellation 55.8 against 58.0 and 57.4 ms summed); 28 views moved over 0.3 ms the same way in both U2 runs, both ways and mostly 3D views (the grass field, area026, lake) that no dock change touches, where the two tip runs alone differ by over 0.3 ms in 72 views (`noise_tip1_tip2.txt`): no view moved beyond the noise. Over the 6.94 ms budget in both U2 runs only the views over it in the tip runs too (area084 under the wheel and with all selected, as in U0's logs). One U2 run failed `reload_frames_at_144` on a single 11.3 ms frame of its second reload pass (median 0.71 ms, as the tip's); the other U2 run and both tip runs passed it (longest 3.4 to 3.9 ms); run alone three times more on U2's final tree (loads 6.0 to 6.8), it passed each time (longest 3.7 to 4.1 ms, `reload_1.log` to `reload_3.log`). **Not built, by the plan**: no panel beyond the area's (none has a feeder yet: decision 2's rule), so no shipped kind has two sections, a floating panel or its own Bottom Dock panel; the wide layout's column seam stays a line (U6); a window's panes' sizes are egui's for the run, not kept. **How the later tasks plug in** (with what the review added: the editor passed to bodies, badges and the late slot, the Preview brought alone, the globals that follow into a window, `owner_of`): **U5** adds `Panel::TileProperties` (dock Right, its body an arm of `panel_body`, available while tiles are chosen) and has `brings_of` give the area a second section, `[[Palette, Preview], [TileProperties]]`, while Select Tiles is on (a second static table chosen by the area's state). **U6** adds `Panel::Properties` and makes the area's table `[[Palette, Preview], [Properties]]` with `folded: [Palette, Properties, Preview]`: `arrange` then gives Main's two stacked sections, Narrow's three tabs and WideArea's Palette and Preview in the first column and Properties in the second (the lone-section rule no longer applies); Q1's double click is `show_dock_panel(Panel::Properties)`. **U12** adds `Reference` and `Help`, a `Tab::Script` arm `Brings { right: [[Reference], [Help]], floats: true, .. }`; docked they fill the Right Dock, floating `window_panes` draws them in the script's window (Floating.png), the script's own side pane retired. **U13** adds `Compiler` and `Bookmarks` to the script's `bottom` (their switches come after the Log's, before the global ones after), and **Search Results** as a global panel: `BOTTOM_TABS = [SearchResults, Log]`, `SWITCHES_AFTER = [SearchResults]`, its hits its `badge`, its availability its feeder's. **U14** gives `Tab::Dialog` `right: [[Node, Data, Search], [Conversation]]`, `floats: true`. **U20** adds **Problems**: `SWITCHES_BEFORE = [Log, Problems]`, a tab in `BOTTOM_TABS`, its errors its badge (`BadgeKind::Error`). A new panel needs its `Panel` arms (`dock`, `name`, `icon`, `tools`, `header_tools`, `strip_tip`, `command`, `keys`, `badge`, `available_with`, `named`'s list) and a body arm in `panel_body` (and in `bottom_dock`'s match only if it draws itself, as the log does); a panel that takes the arrow keys with a `Keys` of its own is named in `Panel::KEYED` (since the review; `keys_leave_panels_not_drawn` goes by what each dock draws).

**Review, 2026-11-15.** An independent review of U2 (its commit `546462ac`) found two faults shown, four suspected and seven gaps later tasks would have had to change U2's code for; the owner ruled on one. Each is fixed below, each new or changed test seen to fail with its fix taken out of the source (the failure text in brackets; the breaks in `target/u2/breaks/run2.py`). **The owner's ruling (2026-11-15): "The area should remember its tab too."** `keeps_fronts` is gone: every kind keeps its section fronts in `Settings::dock_layouts`, the area's too, under the kind `layout_kind` gives (the placeholder that stands for no area keeps the area's). The fault the reviewer found under it is fixed: `section_front` returned `Moonglow::right_panel` whenever the section held it, and that was set to the Palette at start and as a module opened, so a kept front was never read; `right_panel` is now `Option<Panel>`, `None` at start and again as a module opens (with the run's choices), so the kept front is shown. `preview_panel::the_palette_is_in_front_as_a_module_opens` is now `the_area_remembers_the_right_dock_s_tab`: with nothing chosen the Palette, the Preview's tab clicked, the Preview after reopening the module and after a restart (the settings saved and read back) [with the module's reset to the Palette put back: "after reopening: left: Some(Palette), right: Some(Preview)"; the start value alone is not a separate case: every run opens its module through the same path]. The manual says so (02, the docks). **Shown.** (A1) **Two windows' settings**: `Settings::saved_over` merged only the fields this window's text had, and `dock_layouts`, written only where not empty, is missing from a text with none, so an untouched window dropped the other's layouts and undid its Reset Layout. It now merges over every field either text (or the one this window read) has, a missing field a value like any other; files stay byte-identical (the trade: none, the field still left out when empty). `a_window_saves_its_own_changes_over_another_window_s` gains the three cases [the old merge: "theirs taken: left: {}, right: {\"script\": …}"]. (A2) settled by the ruling. **Suspected, each a fault.** (B1) A window's panes were carved bottom first, the bottom pane the window's whole width; the right pane is now carved first, the whole height, the bottom pane under the editor alone (Floating.png); `a_floating_editor_s_panels_are_in_its_window` checks the two panes' places and `a_seam_dragged_keeps_the_sections_shares` measures the right pane's share against its own height [the panes carved bottom first: "[301 520]-[1199 699] beside [920 129]-[1199 519]"]. (B2) `Brings::window_bottom` names the global Bottom Dock panels that follow the editor into its window, after its own (U13: the floating script's Search Results); `a_window_s_bottom_pane_holds_the_globals_its_kind_names` ["left: [Sample 8, Sample 9], right: [Sample 8, Sample 9, Log]"]. (B3) A bare press in a stacked section and F6 wrote `fronts`: they now only move the dock's panel (`focus_right`); a tab clicked, a strip button or a panel asked for by name chooses (`choose_right`), kept; `only_a_tab_chosen_is_kept` [the press choosing: "{\"welcome\": … fronts: [\"\", \"Sample 1\"]}"; F6 choosing: "fronts: [\"Sample 0\"]"]. (B4) `keys_leave_panels_not_drawn` goes by what each dock draws, the Bottom Dock among them, with no panel named in its arms: `Panel::KEYED` lists the panels with arrow keys of their own, each dock's front is the hand-over; the log's keys leave a closed Bottom Dock for the editor, or go to the tab in front; `the_keys_leave_the_log_where_it_is_not_drawn` [the Bottom Dock taken as drawn: "the dock closed"; no hand-over: "to the tab in front"]. **Gaps.** (C1) `panel_body`, `LateSlot` (`editor`, with its `host`) and `Panel::badge` take the editor they draw or count for: the active docked editor in a dock, the floating editor in its window; the floating test checks each body and late body is drawn for `Tab::Manual`, not the docked Welcome page [the editor not passed: "(Sample(0), Window, None)…"]. (C2) A kind may bring the Preview alone (`available_with`: the kind's own where it brings no Palette, else with the palettes); the palettes asked for by name beside it add the Palette alone, no second Preview; a Preview body in a window is salted with its pane (`LateSlot::salted`; the dock's keeps its old `"preview-panel"`), so the dock's and a window's draw in one frame; `a_kind_brings_the_preview_alone` [a duplicate: "left: [Palette, Preview], right: [Palette]"; the Preview bound to the Palette: no Right Dock at all]. (C3) View › Log shows the Log in front of the Bottom Dock and is ticked only while it is (`panel_shown`, `show_panel`); Hide All Panels and the switches open and close the dock as a whole; each tool of the panel in front is enabled as its own command is (`Id::enabled`), not by the log's emptiness; `view_log_shows_the_log_tab` [the old tick: "another tab in front: not ticked"]. (C4) Plugin panels: not needed, by ruling Q3 (they stay tabs or windows). (C5) A window's panes are stops of F6 after the editor area (`Moonglow::window_bars`, the last frame's) and a press in one makes its editor's pane the plugins' pane (`plugin_pane` takes the editor); `f6_stops_at_a_window_s_panes` ["the window's pane reached"], `a_brought_panel_is_its_editor_s_pane_for_plugins` (a press in a floating area's window pane) ["left: None, right: Some(Area(area001))"]. (C6) `owner_of(app, tab)` resolves a tab to the editor it belongs to, whose panels it brings and whose layout it keeps: every tab is its own today, U19 maps the NUI designer's source group to the designer so focusing the source keeps its Right Dock; scripts unchanged (the ruling at T9's review); `the_placeholder_s_layout_is_the_area_s` [the placeholder's own kind: "left: \"no-area\", right: \"area\""]. (C7) The generalized paths (stacked sections, seams, floating panes, Bottom Dock tabs, the switches for several panels, a dock with no available panel) stay covered by the library's tests: they drive the whole `Moonglow::ui` through kittest as the app tests do, and only there can a `#[cfg(test)]` panel exist; no shipped panel yet has those shapes (the area's one section and the Log are covered at the app tier by every `right_dock.rs`, `status_bar.rs`, `preview_panel.rs` and `yields.rs` test). **Docs.** (D1) the Done paragraph's "with no change to what U2 built", its keys sentence and its decision (1) say what the code now does; (D2) the old-reader case of `the_docks_layouts_per_kind_read_and_write_both_ways` reads the newer text with a stand-in struct (`Older`, two fields), as the precedent test does, not with an older build; (D3) 17-plugin-api.md: an area's other panels count as the area's view, in the docks or the editor's window; (D4) `Panel::tools` counts a panel's own list (`header_tools`) instead of a second number; `right_shown` no longer joins the sections into a new list each call (`right_sections` still makes its few small lists: cheap beside a frame, `frame_perf` showed no cost). **Pictures**: the same eight cases, Dark and Light, into `target/ui-mock/impl/m4-u2-fix/`: all 44 the same to the pixel as before U2 (the tip `52d640be`): the ruling shows only once a tab is chosen (the pictures' settings choose none, so the Palette is in front as before), and B1 places only a floating editor's panes, which no shipped kind brings yet. The whole suite and the gates were run after the last edit.

**Done, 2026-11-15.** **Built.** **The Properties panel** (`shell::Panel::Properties`, Right Dock, its body `properties_panel::panel`, its keys `palette_view::Keys::Properties`, in `Panel::KEYED`): a placed object's Properties window's pages without OK and Cancel. `blueprint::edit_many` is split: `form_ui` (with `FormShown`) is the body both draw (the looked-at note and Edit Copy…, the note of several, the page in its scroll, a change refused and said, of several a change only the first would take dropped; it returns where its actions began), and `edit_many` keeps the window's own parts around it (OK and Cancel, the row of pages, `window_drawn`); `object_now` and `looked_at` are shared. The panel never calls `window_drawn`: nothing is noted for a Cancel, nothing closes, and the text it holds is marked `HeldText::panel`, so a Properties window drawn after it in the frame does not claim it. It shows the selection of the area it draws for (`properties_panel::selected`): nothing ("Click an object to see its properties here, or drag a box over several of one type."; the start location alone says how to place it), one object, several of one kind edited together as the window edits them (each field changed set on each, ≠ where they differ, list pages on each), or several kinds ("5 objects of 2 types are selected: …", no fields). Its header (`Panel::detail`, the kit's `PanelHeader` by U2's `section_bar`) says "Placeable", "3 placeables", "5 objects" or "none selected", and holds **Open in Tab** (`open_in_tab_button`, the kit's `open-in-tab` icon) at its end, before the dock's fold button where that is there too (the wide layout's second column): it opens today's `Tab::Instance` or `Tab::Instances`, a tab or a window as Open editors says, with OK and Cancel, on the page the panel shows. While any such window is open on one of the objects selected, the panel says so with **Show It** instead of drawing the same fields twice (two forms of one object would share their widgets' ids, their text buffers and the window's Cancel record: with the guard taken out egui's id check stops the test); the open tabs are read from the dock and from `Moonglow::panes_tabs` (the panes' tabs as the frame began), since a dragged out area's pane is drawn while the dock is out of `Moonglow`. Its pages are the kit's new `PageRail` (`mg_uikit::pages`: 32 px of `bar` with a `line` at its right, 24 px buttons 2 apart from 4 in, `accent-fill` for the page shown, named by their pages in a group "Pages"; it scrolls under the wheel where the section is shorter than its pages and keeps the page shown in sight), each page with its icon (`properties_panel::page_icon`: Basic `info`, Inventory, Lock, Trap, Scripts, Advanced, Variables, Visuals, Description as the Main board, the creature's and the others' from the same set); beside it the page under its name in `section_heading` and, for one object, its blueprint, place and facing ("plc_chest1 at 12.00, 20.00, 0.00, facing 90°"), as the boards draw them. The page shown is kept per type of object (`Moonglow::panel_pages`), so selecting another chest keeps Inventory. A creature's Inventory page stands its item palette over its slots where its room is under 440 points (`creature_lists::INVENTORY_SIDE_BY_SIDE`: the panel at the dock's 280 to 400; side by side the slots were squeezed to a sliver at 320 and drawn over each other, seen in a picture and by the overlap sweep), as before in a wider room. The rail stands flush with the panel's edges (`panel_body` takes `(panel, titled)` and gives Properties no margin); where it shares the one tab bar under 1400 it draws its detail and Open in Tab at its own top. Read-only where the area is held (`claims`), as the window is. **What shows when** (`shell::brings_of`, an area's tab with a module open): with Select Objects, Paint or Terrain, `[[Palette, Preview], [Properties]]` (`AREA_PROPS_RIGHT`; Properties alone without the game's data), folded Palette, Properties, Preview under 1400 (Narrow), the palettes 58 and Properties 42 of the height at first (Main; the new `Brings::shares`, until a seam is dragged), Properties alone in a dragged out area's window (`window_right`: every dragged out area's window now gives its right 280 points or more to the pane, as Tile Properties' did in Select Tiles); with Select Tiles, U5's Tile Properties in its place (its folded order now given, Palette, Preview, Tile Properties, as before), and with Select Tiles and its header toggle off neither (the palettes alone: Select Tiles selects no objects); the placeholder with no area, the palettes alone. **Q1**: a double click on a placed object asks for `Action::ShowProperties(area)` (new, `pub`), run once the frame is drawn (while the editor area draws, the dock is out of `Moonglow` and `active_editor` is `None`): where that area is the active docked editor, the panel in front and the Right Dock unfolded (`show_dock_panel`), in either mode; dragged out, its window's pane shows it. It changes no selection (Ctrl + click twice, a double click, takes the object out again, and the panel then says nothing is selected). The context menu's Properties and Inventory and the module tree's and Outliner's rows keep opening the window. *Changed by the review below: the double click puts its object in the selection, and the rows' double click shows the panel too.* **Q2**: the module tree's area rows keep their arrows (nothing to change). **The wide layout** (WideArea): the area's two sections stand as Palette | Preview tabs in the first column and Properties in the second (U2's `arrange`, its lone-section rule now only for the placeholder); the line between them is a seam (`shell::column_seam`, made after the columns' widgets), dragged to give the first column its width, kept for the editor's kind (`DockLayout::column`, written only once dragged, cleared by Reset Layout, `first_column` holding each column at 280 or more as the dock narrows). **The narrow bar remembers its tab** (the owner's ruling at U2's review): a tab chosen in the one tab bar under 1400 is kept as that bar's front for the kind (`DockLayout::folded`), since the sections' kept fronts could not say which of them was chosen last. **The palette's narrow row** (Narrow, types as a dropdown under 300): Standard and Custom beside the dropdown (the type's name row gone there, kept for the tiles' tileset), the Group by row drawn in the narrow dock whether or not the project offers groupings (Category alone, grayed, where it offers none: else the toolbar wrapped More onto a row of its own at 280), Expand All and Collapse All at its end. **Decided:** (1) **One page at a time**, the window's: the Main board draws one page with its scroll bar, WideArea all of them on one scroll; one scroll is U9's page list for forms, and a creature's fourteen pages drawn every frame would cost the area editor what `frame_perf`'s Inventory view measures for one. (2) **The panel by the tool, not by a selection** (U5's decision 1): it stays with nothing selected, saying how to select. (3) **Under 1400** Open in Tab is in the panel's own top row, not on the shared bar: the one-bar path keeps M3's ids, names and nesting (U2's rule), and a tool on that bar would narrow every tab beside it. (4) **The double click leaves the selection** as the clicks made it (above; *changed by the review below*). **U7. The handles: Fine Lines (1.5 days).**

- **Builds.** Section 11.3 and 11.7 in `overlays`: every line over its edge, the rings as true projected circles of 96 segments, a tilt ring's far half at 40%, the heads, the facing triangle, the scale square and stalk, the pivot dot, the selection box at 1 px over 3, the lit state, the rest of a set at 50% while one handle is lit or held; the spawn point and the start location with the same edge; the grab cursor over every handle (gizmo ruling 5); the name chip on hover (ruling 4).
- **Tests.** Unit: the projected ring against the camera's projection (within half a point); the hit reach and who gets which handle unchanged (the existing handle tests pass unchanged); the cursor over a handle; the name chip's words.
- **Pictures.** `board_gizmo_states` (the States row, on grass and snow).
- **Timing.** `frame_perf` with 32 objects selected and Shift held.
- **Docs.** 04-areas (the handles). Deferred: keeps "Behind things" (1709), "The ring over another object" (2056), "The start location has no Shift axis arrows" (2287), "Marker models unlit" (2221).

**Done, 2026-11-15.** **Built.** The handles are painted by a new submodule, `area_view/handles.rs`, called from `overlays` (no renderer change): a `Canvas` gathers every shape in its layer (the selection boxes, fills, the far halves' edges and lines, the handles' edges and lines, the top marks, the chips) and paints them once, so no dark edge is drawn over another handle's line, as the board's SVG layers have it. **Fine Lines** as sections 11.3 and 11.7 measure it: every line over its edge (black 55%, two points wider; `Canvas::path`), the turning ring a closed line of 96 projected points (`RING_DRAWN`; cut into runs where it passes the near plane, `handles::runs`), its facing a solid triangle on the ring pointing out (8 long by 9 wide, lit 10 by 11) with no spoke, the tilt rings in two halves split a quarter turn either side of the point nearest the eye, the far one at 40% with its edge, the arrows' shafts 1 over 3 to 1.2 r and their heads a line 1.5 over 3.5 to a solid triangle 12 by 8 (lit 2.5 and 14 by 10; a head seen end on draws nothing rather than a degenerate triangle), the scale square 9 (lit 11) over an 11 point edge on a 1 point stalk at 75%, the pivot dot (radius 2 over 3, `#eef0f3`, 70% while a handle is lit), the selection box 1 point amber at 90% over a 3 point edge at 45% (painted with the other boxes, all edges first, in the batched path that turns a large selection into one mesh); selected outlines and spawn posts in the amber over the edge; the spawn point's round tip and square foot and the start location's round tip in the amber, lit in the lit amber and larger; the start location's ring and arrow over the edge. Lit is thicker and brighter (2.5 over 4.5), and the rest of a set draws at 50% while one handle is lit or held (`handles::Lit`: the handle under the pointer, or what a drag holds: a turn every ring, a tilt every ring of its axis, a slide every arrow of its axis, a scale every square; a handle is known by its object and kind, `Handle::same`, not by its shape, so that the ring under the pointer stays lit while Q and E turn the rings drawn before the keys rest). With several objects selected, the handle lit under the pointer dims the other objects' sets too, not only its own (section 11.3 says "the rest of a set"; a drag leads them all, so the one under the hand is the one to see); left so. **The handle under the pointer** is found once a frame by `AreaView::handle_under`, in the press's own order and with its own conditions (a spawn tip or foot, the nearer; with Shift a scale square, an arrow's head, a tilt ring; without it a turning ring; none with Ctrl, the camera's, or Alt, the drag's own raise and turn; else the start location's marker where nothing is picked), where the mode in hand leaves presses to the objects (`Marks::answers`: not with Select Tiles, a paste, Paint's brush, a painting tile brush or the start location being placed); before, each kind lit itself under the pointer on its own, so two could light at once. It lights its handle, gives the pointer **the grab cursor** (ruling 5; a closed hand while any handle is held, the start location's as before) and **a name chip** beside the pointer (ruling 4; bottom-left 12 right and 12 up, the chip of section 11.5 with a strip in the handle's color): "Turn", "Move East or West", "Move North or South", "Raise or Lower", "Tilt (Y Rotation)", "Tilt (Z Rotation)", "Scale", "Turn Spawn Point", "Move Spawn Point", "Turn Start Location", "Move Start Location" (the ruling's two examples kept as written; the tilt rings named by what they do and the field they set, ruling 1; the spawn point's and the start location's by their Undo steps). **Colors** are kit tokens (add-only, `mg-uikit/src/tokens.rs` and the token tables' copy): `handle-x`, `-y`, `-z`, `-turn`, `-scale` with their `-lit` forms, `handle-edge`, `handle-start-ring`, `handle-start-arrow` (Aurora's blue and red), one value in both themes as section 11.3 says (the 3D picture does not change with the theme; the light theme's `select`, `#f09000`, is not the handles'); and the chips' `chip` and `chip-rim`, theme-aware (section 11.5). `the_themes_differ_but_for_the_thumbnails` now exempts `handle-*` as it exempts `thumb-*` (a test changed: the new tokens keep one value by design). **Kept as they were:** who gets which handle, sizes and hit reach (hit tests, grips and `handle_points` still take the rings in 48 pieces, `RING_SEGMENTS`), every drag and key, Escape, the snap; the readouts kept today's white words (U8's chips). **Done, 2026-11-16.** **Built.** **The kit's page list and one scroll** (`mg_uikit::pages`, add-only but for the rail's one-time scroll below): `PageList`, a form's pages at its left as rows of an icon and the name (150 wide with its `line`, 22-point rows 10 in, the icon and the name 8 apart, `panel` behind; the page at the top of the scroll in `accent-fill` and `on-fill`, the other pages in view marked by a 2-point `line-soft` stripe at their left as WideCreature draws them, `hover-row` under the pointer; one group named "Pages" or its own name, each page a button said selected or not; it scrolls where shorter than its pages; Up and Down on a row bring the page before or after to the top, the keyboard going along, as the rail's do); `PageBar`, the bar over each page (26 points of `bar`, a `line` over it but over the first page and one under it, the page's icon in `text-2` and its name in `text`; painted, not a widget: the list names the pages, and a label of the page's name would have stood beside every lookup of it); and `PageScroll`, the pages one after another on one scroll, each in its margins (`PAGE_MARGIN`, the board's 16, 12, 10 and 12), drawn only where in sight. `PageList` differs from U6's `PageRail` in its words beside the icons and its marks of the pages in view, and the scroll is the list's partner (`PageScroll::seen` gives the list the page at the top and the pages in view as the scroll last showed them): a sibling, not a form of the rail. **How the scroll works.** Each page drawn is measured and its height kept; the scroll keeps its place as a page and how far into it, not as pixels, so a page measured anew moves nothing in view: scrolling up into a page never measured (its height the estimate, 400), the place stays held to the page below it until the page above has been drawn and measured, and a page above the held one re-measured has its pass drawn again (`request_discard`), never shown at the wrong place. A page asked for (chosen in the list, or written from elsewhere: Inventory…, the open tabs restored, a test) lands its bar at the top, whatever the pages before it measure, and after the last page there is room to bring its bar to the top too. What is drawn: the pages in sight; the page the keyboard is in, wherever the scroll goes (else egui drops the keyboard of a widget not drawn, and with it what is typed); and in a Tab's or Shift + Tab's pass and the one after (Shift + Tab gives the keyboard over in the next pass) the pages either side, so that the keyboard goes from page to page; a widget it comes to out of sight, by a key or between passes (Shift + Tab, an arrow key), is found among the pages drawn and scrolled into view. Each page is drawn in a room one view high (a page that fills the height it has, Variables' list, fills a view as it did alone) with an id of its own, and each is an accessible group, "Basic page", its bounds the part of it in sight. **The hosts** (`form_pages`, new: `list` puts the list at the window's left, or under `LIST_UNDER` the U6 rail of icons, and gives the room beside it; `scroll` makes the scroll with the pages' icons): a blueprint's window (`blueprint::edit_many`; `form_ui` draws every page on the scroll where `FormShown::all` is given, one page as before where not: the Properties panel), Module Properties and Area Properties (of one area or several; each page's Give Every Area This Page's … Settings now at its top). `blueprint_pages` and `module_page` mean the page at the top: written back each frame unless something asked for another page while the window was drawn, which comes to the top in the next frame (a repaint asked). **The header** (`blueprint::ok_cancel_header`, the `in_header` form of `ok_cancel_saying` of Part 2, decision 4: the same tips and `Pressed`): the kit's `EditorHeader` with the kind's icon, the name and, in `text-3`, the resref at its left (a placed object's blueprint, else its tag; "and 2 more" for several; the module's name and `module.ifo`; the area's name and its resref), OK and Cancel (Close where only looked at) in its end slot; Escape, the closing question, Cancel as one Undo step and a held area's read-only fields behave as they did (their tests pass; where a test's lookups or meaning changed, it is named under Migrated). The other ten callers of `ok_cancel` keep their buttons at the foot until their editors' tasks. **Page icons** (`properties_panel::page_icon`): Module and Area Properties' own added (Events `bolt`, Custom Content `hak`, Visual `light`, Grass `grass`, Audio `sound`). **Found and fixed on the way:** a child `Ui` made with `id_salt` takes the parent's running count into its widgets' ids, so a page's widgets changed ids when a page before it went out of sight and the keyboard was lost (the pages now `UiBuilder::id`); `Context::read_response` takes the keyboard from its widget where a press happened elsewhere in the pass (read only after a key moved the keyboard); egui keeps a scroll's offset under its parent's id, so a window dragged out began at the top (the scroll compares with egui's own state); a page's room followed the sideways bar, which then came and went every frame (the room is the scroll's height); a page laid out one frame wider widened the scroll for that frame (a width counts once the same two frames running); the rail and the list asked for their page in sight every frame where a window at its least could never show it (asked once); the hak list's commands, at their row's right end, stood over its others in a window under 600 (a row of their own there). **Decided:** (1) **The Properties panel stays one page at a time** (U6's decision 1, the Main board's); U6's Done paragraph pointed WideArea's panel at U9's one scroll, but U9's plan builds the scroll for forms only, and the panel drawing a creature's pages every frame is the cost U6 measured: left to the task that takes WideArea's panel, said here. (2) **Under `LIST_UNDER`** (150 + the page's margins + `NARROW_FORM`, 578 points of window) the list is the rail: the list's words would leave the form under the width it is laid out narrow at, where the rail leaves it a window's look (picture: `properties-125-a`). (3) **A field typed in keeps the keyboard when another page is brought to the top** (its page stays drawn), where one page at a time set its text as its page went; a click elsewhere or the window closed still sets it, Cancel still drops it. (4) **The page bar is painted**, the pages' names said by the list and by each page's group. **Done, 2026-11-16.** **Built.** **Sections in columns** (`mg_uikit::form`, add-only): `FormColumns` flows a page's sections into columns, as many of at least 440 points (`metrics::FORM_COLUMN`) with 32 between them (`.form-cols`) as the page's width holds (`form_columns`), the columns sharing the width; each section kept whole, the sections down the first column and on down the next (the keyboard goes in the same order), split where the tallest column comes out least by the sections' heights as last drawn; each section a `Ui` of its own id, so its widgets keep their ids when it moves to another column. `section_heading_with` is the heading with a note painted after it and controls at its right end (the board's Description, "English" and `…`), named "Description (English)" for a screen reader as the label before it was. In the application `blueprint::section` is a heading over a `form_grid` whose labels' column is at least `LABEL_WIDTH` (104), so a page's sections line up. **The creature's Basic page** stands in the board's five sections (Identity; Race and Appearance with the model's warning and Preview; Palette; Portrait; Conversation with No interrupt), two columns in a docked editor at 1600 (Identity and Race and Appearance, then Palette, Portrait and Conversation, as Creature.png), one in a window at its first 980; the Description across the page under them, under its heading. **Statistics** in Ability Scores, Armor Class, Hit Points (Movement rate now in its grid, the separator gone) and Saves: in two columns Ability Scores and Saves, then Armor Class and Hit Points (Creature.png), in one Ability Scores, Armor Class, Hit Points, Saves (WideCreature); the page asks `form_columns` first and orders its sections by it. The creature's Advanced page and the item's General page, which stood in `widgets::two_columns` at 440 and 340, are `FormColumns` of two sections (the other `two_columns` of the blueprints are a palette beside a list, not form sections, and keep U9's restored layouts at 980: a store's palette beside its stock, a creature's slots on one line). **The strref inside the name's field** (`Form::locstring`, every kind's name): "StrRef 24650" (or the language's name, or a StrRef the talk table lacks) is drawn inside the field's right end in the talk table's color and the board's 11 points, a label of its own (named so, its tip kept), the field keeping room for it inside its right margin (`blueprint::FIELD_END_ROOM`, read by `widgets::commit_field`); the field fills its row but for the `…` and the dice (160 to 360 points; a narrow form's 240, held to its room); the languages `…` is a square as high as the field (`widgets::languages_button`, the board's `.field-group > .btn-icon`).
