The Preview's body (`shell::panel_body`, `shell::own_preview` naming the source) is `area_tools::own_preview_body`: drawn in its place, not in the late slot (its form draws no model now), flush with the panel's edges, the arrow keys turning it as the palette's Preview's do (`turn_by_keys`, shared). An area's tab keeps the palettes' Preview of the palette's choice, unchanged but for its header row. **One header row** (`model_view::show`, every model view's: a model's tab, a hak's and a tile's page, both Previews): the kit's `EditorHeader` named `MODEL_HEADER` ("Model header"), Animation (its words painted, the box named Animation, 104 wide; compact without the words, in More with them), Play or Pause, Frame at the left; at the right the missing parts' "N missing" (with their names in its tip) where the blueprint names models the load order lacks, Lights, Shadow and Shaders joined ("Look"), Export Files… (not of a copy), and Pop Out always in More (`Item::in_more`) where it is offered (a form's Preview, a hak's and a tile's page); what has no room goes into More, so the row is one row at 280 (`the_preview_s_header_is_one_row_at_280`). `model_view` no longer reads `icons::Tools` (`toolbar_icons_only`): `Tools::checkbox_word` and `widgets::dropdown_labelled` had no other caller and are gone. **The info line** (`model_view::info`: "c_aribeth: 27 nodes, 18 meshes + 5 parts, supermodel a_fa") is the Preview's `Panel::detail` where it brings its own (the source's name before the view is made, so the bar keeps its form from the first frame); a dock whose one bar is a form's own Preview alone draws its `PanelHeader` (its title, the info line, the fold button) through `section_bar` instead of a tab bar, named "Preview, " and the line (every other one-bar dock keeps its tabs and the group name Right Dock; a floating editor's pane, by `section_bar` as before, is named so too, not "Window's Right Pane"); the kit's `PanelHeader` cuts a detail with "…" before its tools, whole in the header's tip (`mg_uikit::shell`, a change, said: it ran under the fold button; `a_panel_header_s_detail_stops_before_its_tools`). Where the Preview shares a tab bar (folded under 1400 beside palettes asked for), its info line stands over the header in the panel's margin; a model's tab has it over its row as before. **The pages**: `situated::beside_model`, `inline_preview` and `MODEL_LEAST` are gone; a placeable's and a door's Basic page and an item's and a creature's Appearance page draw their fields alone at every width (the creature's "single model" note over them); the Preview button stays (Basic, the item's General and Appearance) and, in the object's own tab or window (`Form::own_tab`, set by `form_ui` where every page is on one scroll), sends `Action::ShowPreview(tab)`: the dock unfolded on the Preview where the tab is the active docked editor, nothing more where its window's pane shows it, else the model's tab (the area's Properties panel, a window too narrow for its pane: `panes_dropped` now keeps any editor's tab, not only areas'). **Pop Out and Bring Back** move from the page to the panel: popped out (the model's tab open), the Preview says "The preview is in a window of its own." (`area_tools::POPPED_OUT`) with Bring Back. **Tools › Preview** beside an editor that brings its own Preview shows it and no longer asks for the palettes (`show_dock_panel`). **Hints**: with a form's own Preview shown (the dock unfolded), the Status Bar gives the Creature board's five (Drag Turn view, Right Drag Move view, Middle Drag Move view, Wheel Zoom, Shift + Wheel Zoom finer: `shell::MODEL_VIEW_HINTS`), after Esc where an Escape would be the tab's own (ruling R1), and not Tab's (the board has none). **Widths** (as ruled at the review, below): a form window with a model asks for 980 + 281 where its Preview pane is drawn (`Moonglow::open_window`), and the pane stands only where the form keeps 972 beside it; in the wide layout a Right Dock of one panel alone is 549 until dragged (`shell::RIGHT_DOCK_WIDE_ONE`, `right_layout_width`: WideCreature's 560 less the 11 points the page list and margins take more than the board's), so at 3440 a creature's pages stand in the board's five columns beside it, Basic, Statistics, Appearance, Classes and Skills heading them. `Moonglow::palette_dock`, the tests' switch, keeps a form's own Preview away too (the inventories' windows laid side by side, and every test of the forms' layout that turned the palettes off). **Seen in the pictures and fixed**: the Preview, taller than wide beside a form, cut a door's sides at 3440 (`ModelView::frame` fitted the model to the camera's 20° up and down alone): it now fits the narrower of that and the width, and frames again as the picture's shape changes while the camera is where Frame put it (moved or zoomed by hand, it stays; `a_tall_preview_frames_the_model_across`). **Renamed or new names:** the row "Model header" (`MODEL_HEADER`); its Animation, Play or Pause, Frame, Lights, Shadow, Shaders, Export Files… and Pop Out keep their names (the tips say what each does, by the style guide); the joined switches' group "Look"; "Missing" (the parts' "N missing"); "+ N parts" goes into the info line; the Preview's header "Preview, " and the line. A creature's or an item's tab with the Preview shown repaints as the model's animation steps (every 33 ms while it plays, as a model's tab always has), where the tab alone was still (2993 ms). The kit test checks the detail is cut, not the tip that holds it whole. **Decided.** (1) The Basic page shows its fields alone at every width, with its Preview button, the 980 window's model beside them dropped: the plan makes the panel the one place for the model, and kept in both the view would be drawn twice a frame once the window has its pane (the coordinator's ruling of U10). (2) A placed object's Properties tab or window brings the Preview of its object too (the inline view showed placed objects); the area's Properties panel brings none of its own: there the Basic page's Preview opens the model's tab, as before. (3) Pop Out in More, not on the row: the board leaves it out, the brief keeps every control. (4) Docked at 1600 the creature's page is one column beside the Preview's 320 where Creature.png draws two of 372: U10's columns are 480 by the coordinator's ruling, which this keeps. **Pictures** (Dark and Light, all seventeen of each looked at, before and after, `target/ui-mock/impl/m4-u11/`): `board_creature` (the Preview with its header row and info line, the five hints, the page one column), `board_creature_wide` (five columns beside the 549 dock, the board's heads), `shell_preview` (the palette's Preview's row at 320, 280 and 420), `forms_wide` (a placeable's and a door's Preview at 3440), the new `forms_floating_preview` (each floating at its first width, the pane beside the form), `blueprint_editors` (every kind at 1000, the Preview's pane saying the harness has no GPU; a window clamped to 85% of a 1000 screen leaves its form about 530 beside the pane, where before it had the whole window). **Tests**: new `preview_panel.rs`'s `the_preview_follows_the_blueprint_s_tab`, `the_preview_s_header_is_one_row_at_280`, `the_status_bar_gives_the_preview_s_hints`, `the_preview_button_and_pop_out`, `a_tall_preview_frames_the_model_across`; kit `a_panel_header_s_detail_stops_before_its_tools`; Pop Out's tests follow (`an_item_s_model_is_its_preview_panel_s`, `a_placeable_s_and_a_door_s_model_is_their_preview_panel_s`, replacing the page's two; `a_blueprint_s_own_preview_keeps_its_view_beside_the_palette_s`, replacing the Appearance page's); changed in meaning: `a_window_opens_wide_enough_beside_its_page_list`, `at_3440_every_page_of_a_creature_is_in_view_in_columns` (five beside its own Preview, not beside a narrower screen), `at_3440_a_list_is_given_its_column_s_room` (Special Abilities is the list given its column's spare: Feats now heads the sixth column over Inventory, the Appearance page being short), `a_placeable_s_appearance_without_a_model_is_said` (the pane says it). Each new or rewritten test was seen to fail with its behavior broken (`target/u11/breaks.txt`). **Deferred** 362, "A preview shown twice in a frame", is restated, not settled: its common case is now a blueprint floating with its own Preview while the palette's Preview beside the area shows the same blueprint; the wording and whether both should draw stay the owner's call. The count stays 229. **Timing** (`target/ui-mock/perf-m4/u11/`: `frame_perf`'s `frames_at_144`, release, the starting tip `1fa72b44` and this change interleaved twice, each run begun at a 1-minute load under 3): the palette's Preview beside an area the same (2.51 and 2.59 ms against 2.57 and 2.63 with the pointer moving, 0.77 idle in both); the new views with a form's own Preview unfolded, its model drawn again as it plays, 1.12 to 1.38 ms (a creature 1.37, an item 1.12, a placeable 1.27), worst 1.68; a blueprint's tab with the Preview beside it 0.1 to 0.3 ms more than without (the creature's 1.21 against 0.90: the model's view); the creature's pages scrolled top to bottom have a worst frame a little worse than the tip's (17.8 and 17.9 against 17.1 and 16.6), the spike the tip has too; all within the 6.94 ms budget. **Next**: U12 to U15 bring their own sections through the same `Brings` (the one-bar `PanelHeader` is the Preview's alone: a kind whose lone panel has a detail extends `right_dock`'s check); a kind's dock of one panel alone in the wide layout is 549; `icons::Tools` keeps its Top Bar use and its other editors' toolbars until their tasks.

**Review, 2026-11-16.** An independent review of U11 (its probes, break runner and outputs in `target/review-u11/`) found these, all fixed in the same change, each with a test seen to fail with its behavior broken (`target/u11/breaks.txt`, "Review round"). **Rulings** (the coordinator's, reversible by the owner). R1: a floating form's Preview pane stands only where the form keeps 972 beside it (`shell::WINDOW_FORM_LEAST`, `window_editor_least`; every other editor keeps its 440): the reviewer measured 530, 568 and 844 at 1280, 1600 and 1920, so there the pane drops and the Preview button opens the model's tab; a new window asks for 980 and the pane only where a pane will be drawn (the game's data read: `Moonglow::open_window`, `Tab::window_size` back to 980); a window of the kind left at a size (U9's 980, often) opens at it and shows no pane unless it is wide enough; manual 05 says so. R2: the header's tips say what each control does, by the style guide, with no "Name:" before it; Shaders' in one sentence. R3: 549 kept in the wide layout (manual 02 says why: five columns of 480 at 3440, four at 560); Creature.png's 380 Right Dock at 1600 is the board's alone (the proposal's tokens and Part 2 give the Right Dock 320), so 320 is kept. **Faults.** (A2) the window's width guarded through the form's room beside its pane, and the pane's absence at 1600 and 1920 and at a remembered 980 (`the_preview_button_in_a_form_s_window`). (A3) ShowPreview's floating branch (the pane shows it: nothing opens) and its narrow-window branch (the pane dropped: the model's tab) tested in the same test. (A4) at 280 Export Files… and then the Look switches go into More before the animation, Play or Pause and Frame (`model_view::show` forces them into More by the row's room, the kit yielding the left group first); `the_preview_s_header_is_one_row_at_280` asserts each item's place at 280 and 320. (A5) the Right Dock's dragged width in the wide layout is kept per kind where the dock holds one panel alone (`DockLayout::wide_width`, `shell::kept_right_width`, `keep_right_width`), apart from the area's two columns' (`a_lone_preview_keeps_its_own_wide_width`). (A6) the header row flush with the dock's own edges, not only the body's (the same test). (A7) the five hints in the board's order, drawn left to right (`the_status_bar_gives_the_preview_s_hints`); a zoom by hand keeps the camera as the panel changes shape (`a_tall_creature_fills_the_preview_and_a_zoom_is_kept`). (A8) Frame fits what the model reaches as the camera sees it, across and up apart (`model_view::fitting_distance` over `Composed::reached_in`, added to `mg-preview`: each mesh's box's corners, a skinned mesh's vertices, rather than the one box round them all), so a tall creature fills a tall Preview: a commoner fills 80% or more of the view's height at the board's 380 (at 320 her width, arms and shadow, holds her to about three quarters). (B3) the kit's `PanelHeader` draws no detail until its tools have been measured (the pass is drawn again), and the tools' width is kept from the first pass even where they have none; its test runs one pass a frame and hovers for the tip (c). (C) Pop Out keeps no ellipsis: it opens a tab, asking nothing (the style guide's rule; Export Files… keeps its own, it asks for a folder). (D) the timing sentence above says the scrolled pages' worst frame is a little worse than the tip's; deferred 362 is restated with the rarer case of two forms of one blueprint (several edited together, and it alone) sharing one view; manual 02's lines on the Preview say the editor brings its own. `at_3440_a_list_is_given_its_column_s_room` runs beside the creature's own Preview as a builder sees it (five columns), Special Abilities under Skills and Spells being the list given its column's spare. **Pictures** (Dark and Light, all seventeen of each looked at, `target/ui-mock/impl/m4-u11-fix/`): `preview_floating_1280`, `_1920` (no pane), `_2560` (the pane beside the form's 972), `preview_docked_1280` (the row at 280), `board_creature` (the creature framed down the panel), `board_creature_wide`, `forms_floating_*`. The full Dark screens run (251 cases) failed six: the five known (`armor_part_none`, `model_viewer`, `nui_saved_window`, `nui_saved_windows`, `update_install`) and `armor_part_pictures`, which was U11's: the item's Appearance page, without its model, is short, and the case's one wheel of 2000 points went on past it into the pages after, so its Right Shoulder pictures were not drawn (it passed three times alone on the tip, failed three times on U11); the case now scrolls a step at a time until the pictures are drawn, and passes three times alone (`armor-parts-shoulder.png`: the shoulder's pictures under the lists). Per-frame work changed only in Frame (on opening and as the picture changes shape) and the header's widths, measured once a frame: no timing rerun.

**After U11's commit (`3add227e`), the page scroll's discard loop.** On U10's tip egui warned that `request_discard` had been called a thousand frames in a row (`mg_uikit::pages`, "a page above the one in view measured"), seen in `armor_part_pictures`' pictures: a page whose height follows where it stands on screen measured anew each time it was placed, and each change had the pass drawn again, every frame for as long as it was in view. The page was the item's Appearance page with its model beside its fields (`situated::beside_model` sized the model by the room in sight under its top, so the page grew each time it was placed above the page held); U11 took that page's model out, and a sweep of every kind's pages (docked at 1200 and 3440, floating at 1000) found no other. The kit now holds such a page (`pages::Flip`, in one column and in columns): a page whose height changes back to what it was at once, or changes in two frames running, is placed at the larger height for 20 frames, so a pass is drawn again at most twice in that time; a single change is taken as measured, as before. Tests: `pages::tests::a_page_whose_height_flips_is_not_drawn_again_every_frame` (a page flipping each pass, and one sized by the room in sight, in one column and two, then grown) and `form_pages::no_form_page_is_drawn_again_every_frame` (the sweep, at most two in the ten frames after each wheel step), each seen to fail with the hold off (the app test with a page sized by the room in sight put back on the creature's Appearance page). `model_viewer` (screens) still fails as on the tip: its repaints are a model view's own (the game's shaders being made, `model_view.rs`, and the window's timers), not a page's discard.

**U12. The script header and the Reference panel (2 days).**

- **Builds.** The Script board's header: Save and Compile with their words; Save As…, Print…, Open…, External Editor; Find… and Replace… as a group; Bookmark; Definition, References, Rename Symbol…, Used By; More (To Scratch); the codepage at the right end; the "modified" label gone (the tab's dot). Right Dock: **Reference** (Functions, Variables, Constants, Templates, the filter) over **Help** (prose with a row per parameter); floating, the window's right pane (Floating). The Right Dock stays while a script's group has the focus (the owner's word at T9).
- **Ticks.** Script Editor "Save, Compile", "Save As…, Print…", "Find…, Replace…", "Bookmark", "Definition, References…", "To Scratch", "Codepage label", "\"modified\" label" (its label), "Functions, Variables…", "Help tab (bottom)"; Floating Editors "Script header, Functions…", "Help tab of the script's bottom pane".
- **Tests.** scripts.rs's side-pane lookups by group, To Scratch through More; new, docked and floating: Reference and Help are one body in either host; `header_holds` down to the least width.
- **Pictures.** `board_script`, `board_floating`, LightScript.
- **Timing.** `editor_perf` (the huge script).
- **Docs.** 07-scripts; parity "Script Editor".

**Done, 2026-11-16.** **Built.** **The header** (`script_view::header`, on the kit's `EditorHeader`, named `SCRIPT_HEADER`, "Script header"): Save and Compile as word buttons marked `primary` (into More last), Save As…, Print…, Open… and External Editor as icons (External Editor disabled without one chosen), a line, Find… and Replace…, a line, Bookmark, a line, Definition, References, Rename Symbol… and Used By, To Scratch `in_more`; in the right group the codepage (`text-3`, 11 points, a `custom` item named by its words, "Windows-1252", with a form in More) and a line, which stays before More. Every control keeps its accessible name and its key; the "modified" label is gone (the tab's dot says it: nothing else read it, neither a test, the plugins' API nor the Status Bar, only the kit sheet's own sample). The header does not read `toolbar_icons_only` (Options' tip: "not the editors' headers"). **Reference and Help** (`script_reference.rs`): `Panel::Reference` and `Panel::Help`, the Right Dock's, each a section of its own with its `PanelHeader` (Reference's detail "nwscript and includes", Help's the name it shows or "Nothing chosen"), `brings_of` giving a script's tab `SCRIPT_RIGHT` (`[[Reference], [Help]]`), `folded` Reference, Help (one tab bar under 1400), the Script board's shares 56 to 44 and `floats`, so that the floating script draws them in its window's right pane (`window_panes`, the same bodies, `Host::Window`). Reference is the segmented control "What to list" (a new kit `segmented_fill`, the board's `.seg.fill`; a list of the four, named so, where the panel is too narrow for their words) over the filter (`SearchField`, F6 to the panel gives it the focus: `Keys::Reference`) and the list; Help the declaration, a parameter to a line (`declaration`), on the editor's ground with a `line-soft` border, then the documentation as `doc_blocks` reads it. The script's side pane, its widest-name measuring and the bottom pane's Help tab are gone (`InfoTab::Help`); Compiler, Bookmarks and Search Results stay in the script's bottom pane for U13. **What brings and keeps the Right Dock**: the active docked editor being a script's tab brings the two panels whatever is open (the game's data or not: the script's own symbols are listed without it); with two groups the dock is the script's while its group has the focus and the area's when the area's has it (the owner's word at T9); folded, it stays folded. **Decided.** (1) The panels are drawn before the editor (the docks before the editor area, a window's panes before its tab): Reference reads the symbols the editor last made (`ScriptTools::symbols`), and what it does is the editor's to do once drawn (`ScriptTools::insert`); the editor draws the frame again where it made new symbols or Help's name changed after them (`ScriptTools::drawn`), so neither hashes the text twice nor shows a stale list beyond one undrawn pass. (2) Help brought forward (a double click on a name in the text, Go to Definition; `ScriptTools::help_forward`) is the dock's to do (`shell::help_forward`), since an editor drawn inside the dock area cannot see the active editor (`Moonglow::dock` is taken while it is drawn): where Reference and Help share one tab bar it moves the dock's panel (`focus_right`, nothing kept); a single click on a name chooses it and leaves the bar on the list, so that a double click can put it in. (3) Help reads as prose, as the plan and the boards ask, against the decision of October that showed it as written (Jasperre's report of lost columns): the markers go (`//`, BioWare's `//::`, `/*` and `*/`, ` * ` down a block, rules), lines join into paragraphs, `- name: text` lines are rows, `*` lines notes, and what is laid out in columns (three spaces or more, the list's later lines from two) or indented under prose is kept as written in the editor's font, so the columns the report was about still line up; a block's shared indentation is taken off. (4) A floating script's pane is never dropped: under twice the pane's 280 it takes half the window (`shell::pane_halves`), as the side lists did, so that Reference and Help stay in reach in an 800 by 600 window (the forms keep U11's rule). (5) Bookmark is a plain icon, as Script.html draws it, not U1's sentence's toggle. (6) (Superseded by the review below: OK and Cancel are at the header's end.) OK and Cancel stay at the foot: neither board draws them, the plan does not list them and the moves table is silent, while decision 4 has each editor's task move them into its header's end slot: the owner's question, **should a script's OK and Cancel move into its header's end slot, though neither board draws them?** (7) Tips say what each control does: Compile "Save and compile the script (F7 compiles all scripts)", Save As… "Save the script under another name", Print… "Print the script through the web browser", External Editor "Edit the script in the external script editor", Find… "Find text in the script (Ctrl+F), the next match (F3)", Replace… "Replace text in the script (Ctrl+R)"; the rest as before. (8) In the wide layout (from 2560) the two sections stand in two columns, Reference then Help, as `arrange` stands any kind's sections (no board draws a wide script). **Records from before** read without a fault (`records_naming_the_old_side_pane_or_help_tab_read_as_before`): no settings field or open-tabs field ever named the side pane or the Help tab (they were `ScriptTools`' alone, for the run); a newer or older layout for scripts naming Help as the Bottom Dock's front or a side list as the folded bar's is passed over, a front not of its section is not taken, and an open-tabs view with fields this version lacks keeps its cursor. **Plugins**: no plugin could add to the script toolbar or the side pane (the API has no such hook); their script commands stay in the text's right-click menu, unchanged; a press in Reference or Help leaves the plugins' pane as it was (`plugin_pane`: no pane of the script's own). **Renamed**: nothing; the panels' strip buttons and tabs are "Reference" and "Help" (icons `book` and `help`), the bodies' groups "Script reference" and "Script help" (`SCRIPT_REFERENCE`, `SCRIPT_HELP`, for a screen reader and the tests: Reference's rows share names with the header's References and the Top Bar's Help). **Tests** (each seen to fail with its behavior broken, `target/u12/breaks.txt`): new `script_header.rs`'s `the_script_header_holds_every_control_from_420_to_1600` (both modes, every 20 points and each side of 796, 962 and 1400, `header_holds` for every control and the codepage, To Scratch always in More, Reference and Help in reach), `reference_and_help_are_one_body_in_either_host`, `help_comes_forward_where_it_shares_a_tab_bar`, `records_naming_the_old_side_pane_or_help_tab_read_as_before`, `the_header_says_nothing_of_unsaved_changes`, `a_small_window_s_editor_keeps_off_its_pane`, `f6_puts_the_keyboard_in_reference_s_filter`; `scripts.rs`'s `help_shows_documentation_as_prose_with_its_columns_kept` (both modes; it was `…_as_the_source_has_it`) and `help_takes_a_block_comment_as_documentation` (prose now); the list's rows looked up by their group (`common::reference_row`), the header's controls through More where they went (`common::script_tool`, `script_click`: the six To Scratch tests of `modules.rs`); `script_reference`'s four unit tests and the kit's `a_filled_segmented_control_fills_its_room_and_keeps_its_words`. Changed in meaning: `the_docks_follow_the_focused_editor_group` (the Right Dock the script's beside it), `the_right_dock_follows_the_active_editor` (a script brings Reference and Help; the manual and Module Properties none), `the_editors_toolbars_show_icons_only_when_asked` (the script's header as it was with Icons only), `thirty_tabs_in_a_narrow_window` (the bar measured again once Module Properties, which brings no dock, is in front). One break was not caught: the codepage's form in More taken away, the sweep still passes, since from 420 points the codepage never leaves the row. **Pictures** (Dark and Light, all seventeen of each looked at, before from the tip's copy and after, `target/ui-mock/impl/m4-u12/`, the before in `before/`): `board_script` (the header as Script_header.png draws it, Reference over Help with ActionMoveToObject chosen: the board's but for the list not scrolled to the name, Help's lines 15 points apart where the board's are 18, and U13's parts), LightScript's the same in the light theme, `board_floating` (the window's header and its right pane, Floating.png's but for the shares, the Script board's 56 to 44 where Floating draws 44 to 56), the new `script_reference_layouts` (As Tabs at 1280 the one tab bar, Reference then Help in front; at 2560 the two columns; floating at 600), and the script cases that showed the side lists or Help (`script_editor`, `script_help`, `script_help_member_and_trailing_comment`, `script_block_help_save_note_and_indentation`, `script_beside_the_palette_pane`). **Seen in the pictures and fixed**: in a script's window 450 wide (`script-800.png`) the editor's bottom pane, wider than its room, was drawn over the pane beside it, and Templates was cut at the segmented control's end: the editor is cut at its room (`script_view::ui`), and where the four words have no room Reference's choice is a list (`a_small_window_s_editor_keeps_off_its_pane`). **Timing** (`editor_perf` release, the tip `cbcc7408` from a `git archive` copy built apart and this change interleaved, tip, U12, U12, tip, each begun at a 1-minute load of 2.7 to 3.0 with the owner's servers winding down, `target/ui-mock/perf-m4/u12/`): the huge script's idle 1.30 and 1.29 ms against 1.43 and 1.29, a key 2.38 and 2.36 against 2.39 and 2.38, the typist's pace 3.14 and 3.17 against 3.14 and 3.10, a new line 3.67 and 3.59 against 3.51 and 3.91; scrolling 1.80 and 1.81 against 1.62 and 1.57 ms median (worst 7.86 and 7.87 against 8.02 and 7.95), a little more each way, the Reference's list drawn beside the text each frame where the old side list was too; all within the 6.94 ms budget. **Not built, by the plan**: the Bottom Dock's Compiler and Bookmarks, Search Results, the live error line as a Status Bar note and the line and column count (U13). **Next**: U13 takes the bottom pane (`InfoTab` and its three tabs) into the Bottom Dock through the same `Brings` (`bottom`, `window_bottom`), and the empty row under the header the live error line keeps; `ScriptTools::help_forward` and `shell::help_forward` are the pattern for an editor that asks its docks for something (its own drawing cannot see the active editor); a kind whose lone panel has a detail draws its header through `section_bar` stacked, the one-bar `PanelHeader` still the Preview's alone. **Reversed in part, 5.2.0 (W5, the owner's ruling on Jasperre's report):** Help is no longer in the Right Dock nor read as prose: it is a Bottom Dock panel after Compiler (a floating script's window's bottom pane), the comment and declaration verbatim (`script_reference::help`, `verbatim`); `SCRIPT_RIGHT` is Reference alone, the shares are gone. Reference, its list and the header stand as built.

**U13. The script's Bottom Dock panels and Search Results (1.5 days).**

- **Builds.** Compiler and Bookmarks as the script's Bottom Dock panels with their switches; **Search Results**, the global panel, fed first by the script's searches (Find In Currently Open Scripts among them); floating, the window's bottom pane; the live error line becomes a Status Bar note and a wavy underline on its line, in both themes; the "Line 17, column 12" count and the last line's 170 cap beside a script.
- **Ticks.** Script Editor "Live error line…", "Compiler, Bookmarks, Search Results tabs", "Key hints" (its count); Floating Editors "Compiler, Bookmarks, Search Results"; Window at 1280 "Log, Problems, Search Results switches" (Search Results).
- **Settles.** "In small script windows the Compiler and Help strip crowds the code".
- **Tests.** The switches open and close their panels; a search's hits in Search Results and a click opening the line; the underline under an error; the count.
- **Pictures.** `board_script`.
- **Hands on.** Search Results to U28 (Find Instance, Find and Replace Text).
- **Docs.** 07-scripts, 02 (the Bottom Dock). Deferred: keeps 1677, 2027, 2033, 1998, 2003.

**Done, 2026-11-16.** **Built.** **The panels** (`crates/mg-ui/src/shell.rs` unless named): `Panel::Compiler` and `Panel::Bookmarks`, a script's own (`SCRIPT_BOTTOM`, `Brings::bottom`), and `Panel::SearchResults`, the global one (`Panel::BOTTOM_TABS = [SearchResults, Log]`, `SWITCHES_AFTER = [SearchResults]`), each with every arm U2 lists (`dock`, `name`, `named`, `icon` Compile, Bookmark and Search, `strip_tip`, `badge`: Search Results' lines found, `available_with`: Search Results always, with nothing open too, as every board draws its switch, `keys` and `KEYED`). Their bodies are `script_panels::compiler` (the script's messages on the board's inset ground, the time in `text-3`, an error in `error`, a click on one with a place going there through `script_view::open_line`, which keeps all three ways of the old `open_other`: the same script, another of the module's opened at the line, a game script read-only), `script_panels::bookmarks` (the numbered bookmarks then the bookmarked lines with their texts, a click going to the line, the empty panel naming Bookmark's key) and `search_results::body` (what was searched over the rows, the rows by `show_rows`, a click opening the hit's own script at its line). The Bottom Dock's tabs stand as the Script board's (Compiler, Bookmarks, Search Results, Log) and the switches Log, Compiler, Bookmarks, Search Results (Problems is U20's); with nothing chosen the dock opens on the kind's kept panel, else the editor's own first (a script's Compiler), else the Log, never on Search Results, the first global tab (`bottom_shown`). Floating, `Brings::window_bottom = [SearchResults]` puts Search Results after the script's two on its window's bottom pane (Floating.png), whose front is the run's (`Moonglow::window_bottoms`, by tab) before the kind's kept one. The script's own bottom pane (`Panel::bottom("script-info")`) and the live error's row under the header are gone. **What brings a panel forward**: `ScriptTools::ask_forward(from, tab, open)` (a compile, a save not compiled, To Scratch, a bookmark set or cleared, a search's hits), acted on as the next frame begins by `shell::bottom_forward` (the editor, drawn inside the dock area, cannot see the active editor, as U12 found for Help): where the asking script floats, its window's bottom pane brings the panel to the front, for every tab of that window (the pane is drawn for the tab in front there); else the Bottom Dock does, a script's own panel only where that script is the docked editor in front, a search's hits whatever is in front; open, the panel comes to the front, closed, the dock opens on it only where `open` says (`focus_bottom`: nothing kept in the settings beyond the dock opened). `InfoTab` and `ScriptTools::info` stay, as the panel asked forward last. **Search Results' state** is `Moonglow::search_results` (`search_results::SearchResults { what, hits }`, each hit a `Hit`, today `Hit::Line { script, line, text }`), fed by `Moonglow::show_search_results(what, hits, from)` (Find All of the Find window, through `search_results::lines_found`; `show_references`); `script_tools::Search::results` is gone. **The live error**: the Status Bar's message (`shell::Shown::note`, a `Note`), in the log's last line's place whether the log shows or not, in the compiler's own words (`hello.nss(5): ERROR: …`: the line said once), in `error`, its tip the whole message and where it comes from, a click going to its line with the keys back in the text; the last line's cap beside a script is the board's 170 (`LAST_LINE_CAP_SCRIPT`). The wavy underline is the kit's (`mg_uikit::marks::paint_wavy_line`, `wavy_line_points`, `WAVE_HEIGHT` 3, `WAVE_LENGTH` 4: add-only), painted over the editor's galley under what is on the error's line (`script_view::error_span`, `paint_error_underline`, its span cached by the text's hash in `ScriptBuffer::error_span`) in the theme's `error`, its middle at the row's foot (the board's `text-underline-offset: 3px`), with the error in its tip in either host; it left the layout cache (`script_layout::LaidOut::text` and `begin` lose the error line: no line is laid out again as an error comes and goes). **The count** "Line 17, column 12" (`shown`'s `Count`) is `ScriptBuffer::place`, the cursor's row and column in the editor's galley (`layout_from_cursor`: a row a line, the text never wrapped), found where the text or the cursor moved. **F6** reaches the Bottom Dock's panel in front, which takes the keyboard's focus from the text (`Keys::Compiler`, `Bookmarks`, `SearchResults`; `ScriptTools::list_focus`; `script_panels::begin` names each body, `COMPILER_MESSAGES`, `BOOKMARKED_LINES`, `SEARCH_HITS`). **Redraws**: every body is drawn before the editor and notes the pass and what it showed (`ScriptTools::made`, bumped by every ask and by kept bookmarks restored; `bottom_drawn`, the least of a pass's); after the frame, `shell::follow_bottom` asks for one frame only where a panel drawn this pass showed what has changed since, or an ask waits, never for a panel not drawn (the endless redraw of U12's review). **Settled** the known difference "In small script windows the Compiler and Help strip crowds the code" (struck through above): the window's bottom pane takes at most a third of the window's height under its tab bar, however far its edge is dragged, and at least its tab bar and a line, 140 points at first (`window_bottom_range`, `WINDOW_BOTTOM_SHARE`, `WINDOW_BOTTOM_HIGH`; its id is the window's editor's, its room cut where the right pane begins). **Decided.** (1) A search's hits (Find All, References) and a failed compile open a closed Bottom Dock (the log says the hits are in Search Results, and a failure must not pass unseen beside its red last line); a compile that succeeds, a save not compiled and a bookmark bring their panel to the front only where the dock is open. (2) A floating script has no Status Bar of its own. The main window's follows the docked editor in front, or a floating window's editor while the pointer is over it or after a press in it (`shell::update_shown`), so a floating script's error is the bar's message then. It also stands at the right end of the window's bottom tab bar, and in the underline's tip in both hosts. (3) The Close Script.png draws at the Bottom Dock's tab bar's end is not built: M3 gave each dock one control that closes it (GitHub issue 10), the Bottom Dock's its Status Bar switch; the bar keeps the panel's tools (the Log's). (4) **The owner's question: should a script's hints drop before the Status Bar's switches lose their words?** The bar yields as M3's T14 made it (the switches' words first, tested stage by stage in `status_bar.rs`): beside a script with all eight of its hints (T12) and Chapter1, the four switches keep their words from 1640 points (measured, the log's last line beside them), so at 1600 they show their icons, where Script.png keeps their words beside five hints; with the board's five hints they keep them from 1400. (Answered at the review below: from 1400 the hints drop first.) (5) Bookmarks keeps today's rows and ways (no names beyond `[n]` and the line's text existed, and removal is Bookmark or F5 on the line, or Ctrl+Shift and the digit again). (6) Search Results says what was searched over its rows; U28 makes the search's form its header. (7) While the live error stands it takes the log's last line's place, so the log's newer lines are not shown in the bar meanwhile (the log keeps them, its switch opens it). (8) A floating script has the Status Bar's message and its line and column count while the pointer is over its window or after a press in it (the bar is the main window's, following that editor, otherwise the docked one in front: `shell::update_shown`). Its error is also at the right end of its window's bottom tab bar and in the underline's tip. **Records from before** read without a fault (`records_naming_the_old_bottom_pane_or_its_tabs_read_without_error`): no settings or open-tabs field ever named the script's bottom pane (`InfoTab` was the run's); was `last_typed`): `references_go_where_the_script_they_are_run_from_is`. **B2**: the asks of a frame are kept as a list (`ScriptTools::forward: Vec<Forward>`); the dock takes the last one it acts on, opening where any of its asks for that panel opens, so the script in front is not lost behind others; the Status Bar's message's tip is the compiler's words and one short sentence ("Click to go to its line."), the underline's the words and "Found as you type." or the include and its line. **Pictures** (Dark and Light, all seventeen of each looked at, `target/ui-mock/impl/m4-u13-fix/`): `script-yields-1600` and `-1400` (the switches' words beside the script, hints dropped at 1400), `script-floating-eof` (the underline above the blank end and the window bar's message), `script-include-error` (the `#include` line underlined), `board_script` (Script.png's words now). **Timing** (`editor_perf` release, tip, U13, U13, tip interleaved again, each begun at a 1-minute load of 2.0 to 2.2, `target/ui-mock/perf-m4/u13/`; the round before, `third/`, had the keys' frames 0.2 to 0.5 ms slower, typing 2.48 and 2.64 against 2.21 and 2.32: `underlined_line` cut the whole script into lines on every key, as the error's place moves with the text, and now goes through its lines only as far as it needs): typing a character 2.33 and 2.18 against 2.21 and 2.16, a new line 3.09 and 3.13 against 3.07 and 3.05, typing after a paste 2.52 and 2.59 against 2.42 and 2.50, idle, the typist's pace, a bookmark, the cursor's moves and composing the tip's within 0.1 ms; **Review, 2026-11-17.** An independent review of U14 (its notes and break log in `target/review-u14/`) held the change's core guards (typed text following its line, Cancel of the panels' edits, Find's own conversation, the panels following the editor, Data's stamp, finding 13.2, the hex field, the header's sweep) and found these, all fixed in the same change, each with a test seen to fail with its fix taken out (`target/u14/breaks.txt`, "Fix round"). **Faults.** (1) A script's or a sound's resref was cut short in its field (the pictures showed `m1q01a01aribsc` for `m1q01a01aribsck1`): `dialog_view::resref_row` gives the field what its row leaves and never less than 16 characters of a name at the text size in use (`name_least`: 16 of the letters, digits and underscore as wide as they average, with the field's margins), the label over the row where the row beside it has not that room (`form_row_least`), and what follows the field (Edit, Play) onto the next line where even the whole row has not (the narrow dock at the larger text); `widgets::with_resref_width` hands `resref_field` that width (`fitted` is gone). `every_conversation_panel_fits_the_right_dock` now compares every one-line field's width with its text's (a name cut short inside its field counts), scrolls each of Data's sections into sight in turn (Actions Taken, Other Actions, Journal entry, Comments) at 280 to 600 and at 20 points, checks the Conversation panel's last row whole, and keeps its one exemption, the preview's code. (2) The read-only test passed with the tree's drop ungated and Import Lines… or Paste enabled: it now presses every command and its keys (Ctrl+V and a paste, Ctrl+A, Alt+Down, Delete), drags a line onto another (a move, and with Ctrl a link), checks Script Wizard… (now off where only looked at: it writes a script and sets it) and Replace All, types in a field, and finds the module never given the conversation. (3) The rest test passed with the Node bar's stamp compared without its pass: it now runs seven cases (As Tabs Data, Search, Conversation in front of the Node section in the one bar under 1400, the dock folded; floating Data, Search and the window's Conversation panel), each typing in its front panel's field, a search run with F3, the selection moved with the keys to Root and back (so that Data and the bar drawn before showed another line and another Bookmark), a line deleted (no selection left) and the delete undone, each settled, and checks that the keys moved the selection. **Suspected, probed.** (5) Ctrl+F over a conversation docked in a group without the focus did nothing and left `search.focus` set: `search_forward` gives that conversation's group the focus (`Moonglow::show_tab`), then its Search the Right Dock's front; where it still cannot show, the ask is let go (`find_over_a_conversation_in_another_group_is_its_own`). (8) What a panel asked for in a frame its editor was not drawn after it is set with that frame's actions (`dialog_view::flush_panels`, as each frame's actions run), never kept for a later frame where the lines may have moved; the editor is drawn after its panels in every frame the code can make (the dock first, then the editor area; a window's pane, then its editor), so it is a guard, tested as a unit (`a_panel_s_edit_its_editor_did_not_take_is_set_with_its_frame`). (6) `follow_unseen` (String Edit following a conversation behind another) took a renumbering without moving what is typed: renumberings are now followed in one place, `follow_view`, as the editor or a panel begins and in `follow_unseen` alike (`follow_typed` takes the context where there is one: without it, String Edit's case, no field has the keyboard, and the parameters being typed are dropped by their field as it is drawn again; no test of its own: a field typed in behind another conversation's tab with String Edit open over it and a renumbering made elsewhere, which no test reaches). (7) The conversation was copied three times a drawn frame: now once a workspace revision, the editor and its panels sharing the copy (`DialogView::copy`, `begin` returns an `Arc<Gff>`); what U15's timing inherits is one copy where something changed and none in a frame where nothing did. **Board differences built.** The script preview's gutter of line numbers, its code never wrapped and scrolled sideways under its own bar with room under its last line; Add Set's ⌄ (the kit's `KitButton::opens` and egui's menu popup); the Speaker tag as one combo, the field and its list's chevron joined, the field never narrower than 16 characters of a tag, its name and the tag typed in kept. **Rulings (the coordinator's).** Data's section headings follow the editor's larger text as its labels do (panel content, not chrome: `panel_heading`, `heading_width`, Script Wizard…'s room measured at that size; the header stays at the kit's size); the Conversation panel's section has the room its rows take at the editor's text size, nothing cut at rest (`shell::section_least`, `section_heights_with`, `dialog_view::conversation_least`: three rows, or as tall as it was drawn last where its labels stand over its fields, `Moonglow::dialog_conversation_height`); Test is one name, "Test", on the header and on the Node bar, its tip "Click through the conversation." (`NODE_TEST`, a `pub` of the first round, removed; tests tell the two apart by their group); "Node" as a title, Bookmarks under Search until U15, the sentence-case renames, the header's text size, the old height record, Toolbar buttons and no yielding at 1280 stand as made. **Board differences kept**: OK and Cancel at the header's end (section 15.2, ruling 10) and the dock's fold button after Test on the Node bar; and at the 320 points of the Right Dock at 1600 a resref's label stands over its field (the board's dock is wider), as 16 characters and the picker and Edit need more than the row beside the label leaves. **The retired lower-pane test's successor**: `a_conversation_s_section_seam_is_kept_across_a_restart` (both modes: the seam between the Node section and the Conversation panel dragged, kept for the kind, and drawn there again in a new window read from the settings). **Tests' manner**: `common::dialog_tool`, `dialog_click` and `conversations::set_commands` settle (and scroll a section's control into sight first) and the hex test waits for its field by a deadline, not a count of frames. **Pictures** (Dark and Light, all seventeen of each looked at, `target/ui-mock/impl/m4-u14-fix/`): `board_conversation`, `conversation-1280`, `conversation-floating`, `conversation-larger-text`. **Found by U15** (2026-11-17): Data got taller as it got wider at 319 to 322 points of dock (332 to 334 at 14 points): `form_row_least` tested the room beside a label without the gap the row puts after the label, so a script's row put its Edit onto a line of its own there, and beside its scroll bar Data never came to rest (this review's rest test had chosen a line shorter than the viewport in both layouts); fixed in U15's review, below.

**Done, 2026-11-17.** **Built.** **Bookmarks in the Outliner** (`crates/mg-ui/src/outliner.rs` unless named): one chooser, `outliner::contents` (`Contents::Area`, T13's panel; `Contents::Bookmarks`, the active docked conversation's), as decision 3 asks; `Brings::outliner` for `Tab::Dialog`. `bookmarks` draws the board's header (Outliner and the conversation's name), the group "Bookmarks" with the bookmark icon and its count (the kit's `TreeGroup`, open at first; named "5 bookmarks" for a screen reader, as the Outliner names an area's kinds, "46 creatures") and a `TreeRow` a bookmark, `fit` to the panel ("Entry 40: Welcome, <FullName>. I r…", the line's kind, number and the first line of its text shown, the talk table's where that is shown), in the order set; none is a quiet row with no arrow and its count 0 (`TreeRow::dim`, as an area's empty kind), its tip saying how to set one. A click or Enter goes to the line (`dialog_view::go_to_bookmark`: `go_to_line`, opening out what hides it), and the click gives the list the keys: Up, Down, Page Up, Page Down, Home, End, Right and Left (open and close the group; Left from a row to the group), Enter, Escape (on the quiet row of none, each does nothing); F6 stops there; the keys' row is brought into sight, so a long list scrolls to it. The keys are `Keys::Marks` with `Outliner::marks_keys` naming whose list (the docked one and a floating one's can be drawn at once); `Moonglow::step_pane` carries each stop's conversation, and `keys_leave_panels_not_drawn` hands them back to the editor where that list is not drawn (and no longer takes the area's `Keys::Outliner` as drawn where the Outliner lists bookmarks). The rows are `dialog_view::bookmark_rows`, which begins as a panel does (`begin`: the bookmarks followed to their lines across a delete, its undo and a change made elsewhere, the deferred entry's rule by its own code, `Renumbering::by_lines`), (The first form stamped the pass and what was listed for `follow_panels`; the review showed nothing it guarded, and it is gone: see the Review paragraph.) Beside a conversation the seam stands where the board has it until dragged (the Outliner 166 high, `OUTLINER_BOOKMARKS_HIGH`), and since the review is kept apart from the areas' (`Settings::bookmarks_panel_height`). **Floating** (the question the brief put): T13 has the main window's Outliner follow the docked editor (a floating window never counts there) and U2 has a kind that floats take what it brings into its window, so a floating conversation's Outliner is in its window, a left pane (`shell::window_panes`, after the right pane, so that what its Node bar did in the frame is listed). ##### M4c: The tables and the rest (U16 to U24)

**U16. The 2DA editor (2 days).**

- **Builds.** The Table board: Save, Add Row with its count, Empty Row, Delete Row, Add Column…, Find, Go to, "N cells are wrong", Values as names and Strings as text at the right, More (Save As File…, Take Rows…, Compact, Show Hidden Columns), OK and Cancel; its own Undo and Redo gone (the Top Bar's); Right Dock **Cell** (value, list or flags, kind words, "Described by" as a note, and the choosers its column kinds have) and **References**; the Outliner of columns (kind icon, kind words, eye); Status Bar "6 cells", "840 rows, 59 columns, in the module" and its hints (Enter Type, Shift + Click Select to, Delete Empty, Ctrl + C Copy, Ctrl + V Paste, Tab Next column, Esc Leave grid).
- **Ticks.** Every 2DA Table Editor row, its New bullets and its first Not Drawn bullet.
- **Tests.** tables.rs's Save, Undo and Redo lookups; new: the eye hides a column as Hide Column does; the Cell panel edits the cell; References finds the row's users.
- **Pictures.** `board_table`.
- **Timing.** `editor_perf` (the large table).
- **Docs.** 03-modules (the 2DA editor). Deferred: keeps 1128, 1154, 1520, 416.

**Done, 2026-11-17.** **Built.** **The header** (`table_view::header`, the kit's `EditorHeader` named `TABLE_HEADER`, "2DA table header", the board's name; reached by the tests through `common::table_tool` and `table_click`, More opened where they are there): Save with its word (`primary`), a line, Add Row and its count joined (a `custom` item: the kit button named "Add Row" whatever its words say, "Add 5 Rows", and the count named "How many rows Add Row adds"; its compact form the icon and the count), Empty Row, Delete Row and Add Column… as icons (eraser, trash, column), a line, Find (the search field named Find, its keys while the pointer is over the table) and Go to (a field named Go to, hint "Go to row", Enter going there), both `custom` and `primary`, so they leave the row last with Save, and "N cells are wrong" where some are (a flat button in `warn` with its warning icon, a click going to the next); at the right Values as names (where a description names values) and Strings as text as one `joined` group "How cells show"; More with its words holding Save As File…, Take Rows…, Compact (a check row), Show Hidden Columns (its words saying how many, "Show Hidden Columns (2)", on only where one is hidden, its tip naming them) and Reset All Widths; OK and Cancel in the end slot (ruling 10). Its own Undo and Redo are gone. A cell refused, a paste or save that failed and the description's folder being read are said in a line under the header (`notes`), where they were in its rows. **The panels** (`crates/mg-ui/src/table_view/panels.rs`, a module of `table_view`; `shell.rs`): `Panel::Cell` and `Panel::References`, every arm (`dock`, `name`, `named`, `icon`, `strip_tip`, `keys`: `Keys::Cell` and `Keys::TableReferences`, F6 giving Cell's Value and References' button the keyboard through `Moonglow::dialog_panel_focus`; `KEYED`; `available_with`; `detail`: the board's "Row 9, TargetType" and "Row 9, Bulls_Strength"; margins and `panel_body`). `brings_of(Tab::Table)` brings `TABLE_RIGHT` (Cell over References), `TABLE_FOLDED` (one bar under 1400), the board's shares (`TABLE_SHARES`, Cell's 372 of 811), the Outliner, `floats`; `pane_halves` holds a table's pane (its choosers must stay in reach); a table's window opens 1040 + 281 + 261 wide where the screen allows (`Moonglow::open_window`). **Cell** (`panels::cell`): its **Value** in the monospace font, typed in (Enter, Tab or a click elsewhere sets it in one step, Escape lets it go; Enter and Escape are taken there, so the grid drawn after neither begins typing nor lets the keys go); its id is its cell's (`value_id`), what is typed kept in `TableDoc::cell_typed` with its cell and the table's count of changes, followed through every row and column numbered anew since (`panels::follow_typed` through the new `Editing::follow`, mg-module, a log of the renumberings of Delete Row, its Undo, Add Row undone, a column taken out, put back or moved): the text, its cursor, the keyboard's focus and the selection go to the cell's new place, and where the cell is gone they are let go of, never set in the cell that took its number; typed for a cell no longer selected (a Go to, the Outliner) it is set in its own; `TableDoc::commit` sets it too (Save, a grid click). Under it by the column's kind: a flags column's names ("Self | Creature | Item | Placeable") and a list's value's name in a second form row; the column's name and its kind's words as a section heading (named "TargetType column: any of 7 flags"); the flags and a list's values as one list of rows with their values at the right (`panels::choice_list`, corrected at the review: one stop of Tab, then the arrows, Page Up and Down, Home, End, letters, Space and Enter, in a frame 8.5 rows high that scrolls; the flags' dropdown gone with `Dropdown::stays_open`); a row's list (`row_choice` at the panel's width); a string's text, Talk Table, Choose String… and New Line… (at the panel's width); a model's layer or its absence and Choose Model… (its note wrapping, the button under it); the column's note, the cell's fault in `error`; at its foot what describes the table ("Described by Moonglow (the game's spells.2da): 34 of 59 columns. A description of yours comes first.", or a file's, "Read again when the file changes"; whose rows its rows are, the description's own notes and the columns it names that the table lacks), or how to give it one. **References** (`panels::references`): Find References to Row N with its icon; it looks on a thread of its own (`panels::find_references`: the table as it is, shared, the game's data and a copy of the module's list of resources, their bytes shared), the stop flag asked between tables (`table_view::references_until`) and between resources (`mg_module::row_uses::row_uses_until`, add-only); "Looking through the game's tables and the module…" with a spinner meanwhile, the window going on and `under_way` counting it; stopped as another row is chosen, the table changes or the table closes (`Looking`'s `Drop`); then "In the game's tables (8)" and "In the module (3)", each a row with its icon (a table's, an object's kind, a resource's type), the module's links going there, two hundred of each listed and the rest counted; "Nothing names row N" where nothing does. **The Outliner of columns** (`outliner::columns`): its header "Outliner" and "59 columns" with Show Hidden Columns' eye at its end; a `TreeRow` a column in its order, its kind's icon (`panels::kind_icon`: a list's, flags', a talk-table string's, a script's, a row's table's, else the column's) and its kind's words weak after its name (`panels::kind_words`, the description's, else what the checks know of the game's table; said with the name to a screen reader: "Kind, one of 2 values"), quiet where hidden, and its eye ("Show Kind", on while shown), which hides the column as its menu's Hide Column does (`TableDoc::hide_column`, which both now call) and shows it again; the selected cell's column marked. **Review, 2026-11-17.** An independent review of U16 (its notes and probes in `target/review-u16/`) found these, all fixed in this change, each with a test seen to fail with its fix taken out (`target/u16/breaks.txt`, "Fix round": batches F1 to F22). **Faults shown.** (1) **The grid kept its keys for an editor not in front**: Tab, the arrows, Delete and typing reached a floating table's grid after a press in the main window, and Tab was kept for a read-only view in front of its pane whatever editor was active (`browser::view_in_front`). The grid's keys are now its table's only while that table is the active editor: `table_view::grid_has_keys` (the keys the grid's, of this table, `active_tab` its tab, nothing modal) for the grid, its hints, Undo's keys and `keep_tab_for_the_grid`; `Moonglow::active_tab_now` is read as the frame begins (the dock is taken out while its tabs draw); a read-only view passes its own tab (`browser::view_tab`, in place of `view_in_front`); a click on a cell asks the dock's focus for its tab (`focus_asked`, applied once the dock is put back). `the_grid_s_keys_are_the_active_editor_s` (docked with another group pressed, String Edit open, floating with the main window pressed, Shift+Tab, a popover) [F1: "floating, the main window pressed: the selection as it was"]; `a_table_only_looked_at_says_whose_it_is` now presses a blueprint's view in another group and holds spells' cell, and `a_floating_table_only_looked_at_lets_go_of_its_keys` presses the main window beside a view in a window of its own (As Floating Windows: a view floats too). A press in another editor, docked or in the main window, already takes the arrow keys from a view's grid itself (`keys_are` no longer the table's), so breaking the view's gate alone (F2, F2b, F2c) fails nothing: the gate is kept as the editor's, the tests hold the behavior. (2) **Enter in Cell's Value copied the whole table** (it was set while the panel held `edit.shared()`): it is now set after the panel lets go (`panels::cell_body`); `the_cell_panel_edits_the_cell` holds the table's `Arc` pointer the same [F3]. (3) **A list's and the flags' rows were each a Tab stop**: they are one list (`panels::choice_list`: one focusable list named "Values", its rows clicks; Up, Down, Page Up and Down, Home, End, letters, Space and Enter; a frame 8.5 rows high that scrolls, the cursor's row brought into sight). `a_long_list_is_one_list_with_its_keys` (300 values: one Tab, End, a letter, Page Down, Space; the panel stays short) and `tables::a_flags_list_is_ticked_by_the_keys` [F4]. (4) **The grid's keys under the header's More** (found by the popover case asked for): the arrows moved the grid's cell with More open, the kit's popovers not being egui's popups (`shell::keys_blocked` sees those): `grid_has_keys` asks `Popover::any_open` too [F12]. (5) **A list's value out of sight** (found in `table-long-list`): shown for another row's cell, the list kept the keys' row of the last; its row is now kept with it, and for another row's cell the keys' row is the first one on, brought into sight (`a_long_list_is_one_list_with_its_keys`, a second row's value 240) [F13]. (6) **F6 left the keyboard's focus where it was** (found by the F6 case asked for below): from References' button F6 gave the Outliner the keys while the button kept the focus, so its arrows and Enter did nothing (`tree::keys_free`; the same from Cell's Value, and docked with a module at the Module panel): `Moonglow::step_pane` lets go of the focus at every step, a stop that takes it asking again as it is drawn [F20]. (7) **The cursor on a wrong cell, in the light theme**: its red text on `accent-fill` read poorly (`table-wrong-cursor`): the cursor's text is `on-fill` whatever the cell, the wrong cell keeping its red outline. (8) **Guards**: `follow_panels` and the panels' pass stamps had no case that needed them (a break of them failed nothing): taken out, as U15's stamp was; typed text set by its old number where Cell is not drawn (`typed_text_is_set_in_its_cell_where_cell_is_not_drawn`, folded and behind References) [F5]; a read-only view's hints that change a table checked absent with its grid's keys [F16]; `the_cell_panel_follows_a_table_read_again` [F15: the table not read again; a missing repaint cannot fail it, kittest's runs always draw a frame]; `common::table_headers_with` fails where no header is drawn (it counted the kit's records of the last pass that drew one; a probe, taken out after). **The board's grid** (the coordinator's word: built now): the header row 24 high on `bar` with its lines, the cursor's column's name in `accent`; the gutter `bar`, its numbers monospace 12 in `text-3` at its right with 8 to spare, a line at its right; `cell-line` at each cell's right and foot (drawn once a row and once a column, `table_view::look::Lines`); cells chosen together `cell-range` (new: the board's `.c.rng`, light made as far from its panel); the cell with the keys `accent-fill` with `on-fill` text and an inset `accent` ring while the grid has the keys; no outline round the whole grid (`keys_outline` gone for the grid); the Cell section heading bold. A read-only view's grid is the same code (`table_view::grid_in`), and `table_view::look` (`header_cell`, `gutter`, `number`, `cell`, `Lines`) is there for U17's talk table. **Rulings (the coordinator's).** With no module open, docked, the Left Dock is drawn whenever the Outliner has contents for the editor in front, holding the Outliner alone, its fold button at the end of its header, folded to a strip of its icon (`shell::outliner_alone`, `left_holds`, `outliner_alone_ui`, `outliner::alone`): only a table qualifies (an area's and a conversation's Outliner want a module); `a_table_without_a_module_lists_its_columns_in_the_left_dock` (F6 stops there once: Shift+F6 from the grid, again, back, Down and Enter, F6 to the grid; `step_pane` had made the Outliner alone two stops) [F6, F7, F19], and `the_left_dock_of_other_editors_is_as_before_with_or_without_a_module` (an area, a script, a conversation and a blueprint with a module; the game's script and blueprint without), which passes on the tip too (run in the tip's copy) [F14]. U16 costs about 0.18 ms a frame over the tip (the first round measured 0.15, on a quieter machine). Where it goes (`parts/`: the same binary with temporary switches, since taken out, leaving out one part at a time): the board's grid nothing measurable (its lines drawn once a row and once a column, `look::Lines`, the tokens read once a pass; drawn two to a cell, a first pass on a busier machine read 0.82 to 0.99 ms), the Outliner's columns about 0.06 ms (only the rows in sight, `show_viewport`, the kinds' words kept by `columns_mark`; it had laid out all of them), Cell and References about 0.03, and about 0.08 left with all three out, which these runs did not take apart (the kit header row and the Status Bar's hints and counts are what else U16 draws: inferred, not measured). The popover gate, the list's row kept by cell, F6's focus and the cursor's text came after these runs (a lookup a frame, no more drawn); the tip's copy is deleted. **Probed and tested.** A floating table's header beside its panes (`a_floating_table_s_header_beside_its_panes`, the pattern of U15's): in a new window in a 1280 by 720 screen and a kept 1100 by 700 one, the Outliner gives way first (its strip) [F11]; the right pane stays, and beside it Add Row goes to its compact form in the new window (its words kept in the kept one), every other item where the board puts it. Delete and the arrows in an area's view beside a table whose grid had the keys, docked and floating, act on the view and leave the table alone (`area_view::the_area_s_keys_beside_a_table_that_had_the_grid_s`) [F10]. The Outliner lays out only the rows in sight (`the_outliner_lays_out_only_the_columns_in_sight`, 160 columns: End, letters, Enter, Home, a click) [F8, F9], its kinds' words kept by the table's mark and the load order's count (`Moonglow::load_order`), made again as the description is read again (`the_outliner_follows_its_description_read_again`) [F21] and as the game's data is (`the_outliner_follows_the_game_s_data_read_again`: a module kept as a folder given an `itempropdef.2da` from outside that names a table of ours) [F22]. **Board differences kept**: the kit's scroll bars, the first column's widths, the dock's fold chevron after Cell's detail, the Outliner header's eye lit only where a column is hidden, the Problems switch (U20), and a floating table's right pane kept while its header yields (above). **Pictures** (Dark and Light, all seventeen of each looked at, `target/ui-mock/impl/m4-u16-fix/`): `board_table`, `table-1280`, `table-floating`, `table-floating-strip`, `table-floating-strip-open`, `table-read-only`, `table-read-only-cursor`, `table-no-module`, `table-long-list`, `table-wrong-cursor`. its lines numbered by their own StrRefs (`Which::strref`), Go to by them, its CSV export by them (`Table::to_csv_as(false)`). Nothing changes it: Add Line, Remove Last Line, Save and the imports off, Close alone, String read-only, the Status Bar's "112228 lines, read-only". **Hints and counts** (`panels::shown`, through `shell::shown`): "30 lines" ("…, read-only" for a table only looked at), and while the list has the keys and nothing is typed, Up / Down Choose line, Page Up / Page Down By ten, Enter To its text, Double Click To its text (always), Esc Leave list, each as bound (fixed keys); none while a modal, a dialog, a menu or a kit popover is in front; they yield as every hint does. **No endless redraw**: no stamp; Find and References are followed every frame whatever is drawn (`talk_view::follow`, beside `table_view::follow_looks`), which a rest test found missing (References with String in front never ended); the module's view lets go of its look and its Find where its table is gone or its tab closed, the game's table goes as the tab shows another table or closes. **Decided.** (1) **`dialog.tlk` draws in the Talk Table tab**, as the board draws it (the owner's ruling, 2026-11-17; it was first a tab of its own, `Tab::GameTalkTable`, titled "dialog.tlk", by the coordinator's ruling): the module's table (its typed lines, Undo steps, chosen line and scroll) waits behind it untouched and is back with More › Module's Table; opening the game's never asks to save or drop the module's. (2) Its lines are a copy made once at its opening (`Arc<Table>`), not read through the game data each frame: the editor's find, list and export work on a `Table`, and the copy is never made again while the game data is the same (its place, its table's place and length: not a weak pointer, which would keep the window from changing the game data in place). (3) String's fields are set as they are typed, a burst one step (as the old editor's were), rather than kept and set as the field is left (U16's Cell): nothing waits to be set, so typed text cannot land on another line nor be lost where String is not drawn; the fields' ids are their line's. (4) Find References in the header runs the References panel's look, not the Find References tab (which a StrRef typed in its field still opens, as before); the panel finds what the tab finds (the module's fields, scripts, 2DAs and sound sets, the haks' 2DAs). (5) The game's table's References look in the module and its haks as the module's do (its StrRefs as the files have them, from 0); the game's own 2DAs are not looked in (U16's References for a table did; a dialog.tlk line is named by hundreds of the game's cells). (6) The tab with no table of its own keeps the header (More's Open File… and New File…) and says where to make one; the page that makes one is the Talk Table panel's Module's Table, as the board draws it. (7) Read-only: the board draws Add Line, Remove Last Line and Save off rather than absent; the imports are off in More; String's fields are read-only text that can be chosen and copied; no hint says what the table cannot do. **Plan against board**: (1) withdrawn: `dialog.tlk` draws in the tab titled "Talk Table", as the board draws it (the owner's ruling, 2026-11-17); (2) `Talk_header.png` draws Undo and Redo; `Talk_fix_header.png` and `Talk_fix_hdr2.png`, drawn after it, have none, as the plan: none; (3) `Talk_right.png` draws Play beside Sound, which `Talk.png` and its source do not and the plan does not list: not built (nothing plays a sound from the editor today);
