**Review, 2026-11-19.** An independent review of U23 (its evidence in `target/review-u23/`) found the faults below; each is fixed with a test seen to fail with the fault put back (`target/u23-fix/breaks.txt`). (1) **A floating read-only tab** gave the Status Bar no resource or count: `shell::update_shown` now takes the floating editor under the pointer, else the one clicked last (`tabs::Viewer` reports each), and the lock alone carries "nw_chicken.utc from key:nwn_base, 3078 bytes, shown as the game reads it" in its tip (the kit's `Item::custom` ignores `.tip()`: it is put on by `ui.interact`). (2) **Copy Value copied the shown text** ("31  Chicken"): it copies the value itself (`ro_gff::value_copy`: a string unquoted with its line breaks, a resref, a number, a void as hex); a locstring's item says what it copies ("Copy English Text", "Copy StrRef"), Copy All Languages where it has two or more, Copy Meaning where a row has one; Ctrl+C (the backend's Copy event) on a focused row copies its value; Shift+F10 opens the menu with its first item focused, Tab moves, Enter copies, Escape closes it and gives the keyboard back to the row. egui and egui-winit have no menu (ContextMenu) key, so Shift+F10 is the keyboard's way; the menu bar's F10 had taken Shift+F10 too (`consume_key(Modifiers::NONE, F10)` matches Shift loosely) and now takes F10 alone. With item 2 the ruling on drag-selection holds: text is no longer selected by dragging, accepted. (3) **Enter while Options › Keyboard waits for a key** was OK: one rule, `shell::enter_is_ok(recording, ctx)`, now decides the hint and OK, so Enter is recorded as the key; Escape gives up the waiting alone (both tested through the real "Add a key for …" button). (4) **Questions over their dropdowns at the board's setup**: the columns are the board's 380, 336 and the rest with gaps of 24; Options is flush in its pane as the board draws it (`tabs::form_window`); the label column is the board's 186 and gives its spare room down to the longest label (177) before a label goes over its dropdown, which is only where the dropdown cannot hold its longest choice whole (`question_least`, measured from the twelve choices: 182). The minutes field is 44 wide without spin arrows (the board's `.inline .num`; `widgets::name_next_field` from the first round is gone with its last reader). The test harness puts the app in a panel with egui's 8-point margin, which the real window has not: the board's 1600 is tested at a 1616 harness, and the harness's own 1600 too. Not a break: with the tabs' 6-point margin back, the third column is exactly the 372 it needs and still passes. (5) **The OK/Cancel test** counted OK's press, and apply twice where a change reloads: `options_applied` counts where settings are applied (`apply_options`, or OK's looks-only branch), the settings writes are counted as the frames where they change; one control on each of the ten pages (the theme and interface size among them) is set by OK and set back by Cancel, Escape and the tab's ×, docked and floating. (6) **`read_only_counts`** read only the tab's trees: one thread-local count of every listing of a `ro_gff` tree wherever drawn (`ro_gff::counts`); the hak Preview's GFF lists its rows once a fold (`the_preview_s_gff_lists_its_rows_once_a_fold`). (7) **Wrong words for none**: `ro_gff::missing` says nothing for what `mg gff --names` prints nothing for, by `mg_rules`' own knowledge (StrRef none, a number below 0, the field type's largest, the row no table has, a row present with a blank or `****` label: `GameData::row_name`), and "(no row N in T.2da)" only for a row the table lacks; a custom StrRef with no module talk table read says "(string 5 of the module's talk table, not read here)", with it read, its text. The view's meanings over the reviewer's 21 game files match their `mg gff --names` output with no mismatch (`target/u23-fix/xcheck/cmp.txt`). (8) **The lock alone** is reached in the app: docked at 1600 with both docks open at ×1.25 and ×1.5 (tested there, with its tip), and in a 760-wide window (`resource-narrow-760`). (9) **New tests**: the tab's × sets Options' changes back (in the OK/Cancel test); closing the main window with Options changed (its X then Close Moonglow, and File › Exit) sets nothing, the draft going with the window as at the tip; every opener lands on its page: Tools › Options… (`Id::Options`) and the Welcome page's Options… with no game data open on Folders, and the kept tabs reopened with the module open Options on their page (`open_tabs`, `windows::side_editors_and_tools_open_again_with_the_module`); Copy to Module on a hak's copy of a 2DA puts that hak's bytes in the module (one Undo step), a texture (no editor) lands with one Undo step, no tab, kept by Save; a module kept as files (a folder or nasher project) names a resource by its kind's extension, so a kind with none was written as `name.#id` and lost on reading back: Copy to Module is off there with the tip "A module kept as files cannot hold this kind, which has no file extension" (an archive takes it). A picture of the read-only tab in the narrow layout: `resource-narrow` (1000) and `resource-narrow-760`. **Board work.** `board_resource`: the tree scrolled to SkillList, struct and list counts muted in body text, the log's last line cleared as the board's bar has none, so the hints are whole with Ctrl + F Find last (bound: Find's key goes to the Name field with the pointer over the panel); the outline round the Resources list is Moonglow's own rule, `palette_view::keys_outline` (the pane holding the arrow keys), not the kit's, kept although the board draws the list's key hints without it. `board_options`: Questions beside, the minutes field without arrows, the pointer in the page list's empty room, the creature tab closed and the module tree from its top as the board's; Scripts stays open because Show the tab chosen in the module tree reveals the open script, which the board's fixture folds. Pictures, Dark and Light: `target/ui-mock/impl/m4-u23-fix/`. **Rulings** (words only): drag-selection loss accepted with item 2 done; long values cut, whole in the tip, accepted; folds kept per layer copy, accepted; pictures and sounds shown as hex are not U23's (no deferred entry); GFF rows have no arrow keys, accepted; Save As has no guard on its target, no change; the "Esc Cancel" hint is kept although the board lacks it (plan against board, R1). **Timing** (`frame_perf::read_only_and_options`, the fix round against a fresh copy of the tip 79a0ef8c, interleaved over three rounds, each run at a load under 3): the GFF view, all 2,100 fields unfolded, 0.17 ms against 3.28 (medians, the pointer over it); Options' General 0.23 against 0.20 (17,112 vertices against 12,504); the worst single frame 0.40 ms, budget 6.94 met (`perf-m4/u23-fix/summary.txt`). The full Dark screens run (`target/u23-fix/fullscreens/run.log`): 261 passed, the five known failures alone (armor_part_none, model_viewer, nui_saved_window, nui_saved_windows, update_install). Gates: fmt, the three clippy lines clean, the workspace's tests 4,491 passed and none failed, doc tests 18, `mg-uikit --features dock` and `mg-plugin` passed, `okf lint docs --links` clean; the deferred count stays 229.

**U24. Welcome and the empty editor area (1.5 days).**

- **Builds.** The Welcome board: the heading with the version; Recent Modules with the path as a weak line (finding 13.3 fixed); Start (icons and keys); "Without a module"; Status ("Game data found", Options…, the update's buttons); Learn (User Manual and the chapters); Help (Command Palette…, Check for Updates…, About); the drop note. "No area open" as a centered `EmptyState` with Area Wizard… and Go to Start.

- **Tests.** Each Start, Without a module and Help row runs its command; a recent `.nwm` has no "/" after it (a test seen to fail first); the empty state's two buttons.
- **Pictures.** `board_welcome`. **Docs.** 01-getting-started. **Merge point M4c.**

**Done, 2026-11-19.** **Built.** **The Welcome page** (new `crates/mg-ui/src/welcome.rs`; the old `tabs::welcome`, `recent_entry` and `no_area` gone): laid out from one plan (`welcome::plan`, a list of parts with their rectangles, then drawn), in three columns at the board's shares (1.45 : 1 : 1, gaps of 40, the board's 40-point side less the tab's 6) where each has its least width (280, 260, 200), two (Recent Modules and Learn, Start and Status) where those have, and one column under 560; the page stands in the middle of its room where it fits and scrolls in the tab where it does not, and a test holds that it is never taller where it is wider (`the_page_is_never_taller_where_it_is_wider`, 300 to 2000 points at 100, 125 and 150%). **The heading**: "Moonglow Toolset", the version and the line, the line under the name where the row has no room. **Recent Modules**: the name, a `/` after a folder (a `.mod` or `.nwm` file in any case has none; finding 13.3), and the folder it is in as a weak line with `~` for the home folder, cut with an ellipsis, the whole path in the tooltip; each row focusable, named "name in folder" for a screen reader, opened by a click, Enter or Space; only the rows in sight are laid out and painted (two hundred recent modules: the rows of one screen), every row taken for the keys, so Tab goes through them all in order and brings each into sight as it takes them (Learn's links the same); a row's id is its place in the list (a list edited by hand can name a module twice), and a module with no folder (a bare name) is named without "in"; "No module opened yet." with none; the drop note under it ("Also in File › Recent Modules. A module file or folder dropped on the window opens too."), made true: a single folder dropped with no module open that the module reader takes for a module opens as the module (`transfer::dropped_to`, `holds_module`: a `module.ifo` in any case, as a folder's files are read, or a nasher project's `nasher.cfg` by that very name); with a module open it is imported, as before. **Start**: New Module…, Open Module… and Open Folder… as the board's wide rows with their icons and their keys as bound (none where unbound), the key told to a screen reader as the row's shortcut (the kit's `KitButton::keys`, `at_least`, `quiet_icon`, `height`). **Without a module**: the eight commands two by two where each fits its half, else one by one. **Status**: "Game data found" and the game's folder, or what to do with none, and Options…; the update's line (`updates::line`, every state of the notice: available with What's New…, Install Now (the main button) and Later, or Release Page where Moonglow cannot install itself; downloading with a spinner and its count; ready with Restart Now; failed with Try Again and Release Page; "Checking for updates…" with a spinner), not drawn while the Check for Updates window tells of the same release (the strip's rule; `updates::act` runs its buttons). The strip under the Top Bar is drawn from the same `updates::line`, with Don't Remind Me and its Close added: one reading of the notice's state for both. **Learn**: User Manual, the board's sixteen chapters in its order as links, each opening the manual on its own chapter (`manual::open_chapter`), and Help (Command Palette…, Check for Updates…, About Moonglow Toolset). **The strip under the Top Bar** is not drawn while the Welcome page is in front of its pane and its update line was wholly in sight, under no window but a dialog, at the last pass (`welcome::in_sight`, `welcome::Kept`); where the page was not drawn in front at the last pass (the first frame, another tab in front before) the line is taken as in sight. Where the page scrolls the line out of sight, wholly or in part (the log open in a short window), or a window stands over it (a floating editor; not a dialog, About or Check for Updates, which would move the page as it comes and goes), the line and its buttons are not drawn and the strip tells it, so it is told once; where the page finds the strip took it wrongly, the pass is drawn again (`request_discard`), so no frame shows both or neither, and the strip's room given back only brings the line further into sight (the two never take turns). The Check for Updates window's not-installable branch gained Don't Remind Me About This Version. **No area open** (`welcome::no_area`): the kit's `EmptyState` with the map icon, "No area open", "Double-click an area in the Module panel, or find one with Ctrl+P." (the key as bound, else Quick Open) and Area Wizard… and Go to Start (off where the module has no areas). **Hints and counts** (`shell::shown`): the page's hints go while a menu or another window takes the keys, and no row, link or button of the page acts by the keys while a menu, a dialog or a modal has them. The section headings and the two sub-headings (Without a module, Help) are headings to a screen reader. No area open walks the module's areas once for each change of the module (by the workspace's revision), the chapters' titles are found once, whether a release installs is checked once for each release and setup, and a folder dragged over the window is read once for the drag (`Moonglow::welcome_counts` counts them). Each button of the page sits in an id scope of its own, so its id and the keyboard focus stay as the update line comes and goes.

**Plan against board** (Welcome.png, `Welcome_crop_recent.png`, `Welcome_crop_start.png`, compared with `board_welcome` at 1600×900, Dark and Light, in `target/ui-mock/impl/m4-u24/`): the heading at the board's height, the three columns at its x positions to within the harness's 8-point margin, the rows (43 high), the section rules, the Start rows with their keys, Without a module two by two, the Status lines and buttons (Install Now in the accent), Learn's links and Help as drawn. **Review, 2026-11-19.** An independent review of U24 (its notes and breaks in `target/review-u24/`) found the faults below; each is fixed with a test seen to fail with its fault put back (twenty-two breaks, all caught at the end, the misses on the way told: `target/u24-fix/breaks.txt`). (1) Recent rows below the fold could not be reached by the keys: the rows out of sight were skipped, so Tab went from the last row in sight to New Module…, and a row taking the keys half under the Status Bar was not brought into sight. Every recent row and Learn link is now taken for the keys (a bare `interact` out of sight), laid out and painted only in sight, and brought into sight as it takes the keys (`tab_reaches_the_recent_rows_past_the_fold`: Shift+Tab from New Module… to the two hundredth row, then Tab through all two hundred, each in sight, fewer than forty laid out). (2) With floating editors a window over the page's update line hid it, and no strip told it: the line counts as out of sight when any window's rectangle covers any of it (`a_window_over_the_update_line_has_the_strip_tell_it`, the Manual over the line at 1400 by 800), except a dialog's (`widgets::is_dialog`): About standing over the line (at 900 by 900, and from 600 to 1000 points wide in windows 800 to 1100 high) brought the strip in and moved the page, fault (4) by another way, so a dialog is not counted (`a_dialog_over_the_update_line_moves_nothing`). (3) No area open read `module.ifo` and walked the module's resources every frame to enable Go to Start; it is now kept by the workspace's revision, and one counter (`Moonglow::welcome_counts`) counts every walk, chapter-title scan, check of whether a release installs and dragged folder read of both pages, and the passes the page throws away (no other file-system call, environment or settings read is made per frame: the home folder is looked up once, a recent module is told a file or a folder by its name, and the keys shown come from the keymap in memory) (`the_pages_walk_scan_check_and_read_once`: none in twenty frames of each page, one read of a folder dragged for ten frames, one walk after a change). (4) Check for Updates… from the page made the line vanish and the strip appear, so the page jumped 13 points: by the ruling, `updates::line` hides the line only while the window tells of the same release, the strip's own rule (`check_for_updates_from_the_page_moves_nothing`). (5) Enter on a focused recent row opened the module under About: no row, link or button of the page acts by the keys while a menu, a dialog or a modal has them, and a click of the pointer on the page beside a dialog is still the page's, as anywhere else in the window (`a_recent_row_opens_nothing_under_a_dialog`, under About and under Check for Updates: Enter on a recent row, a Learn link, Options… and What's New… does nothing, a click on Getting started beside the dialog opens it). (6) Three tests passed with their fault: the told-once rule is tested with the line half in sight at the page's top, under the tabs (`an_update_line_half_in_sight_is_the_strip_s`; at the bottom edge the strip's going gives the page more room than the line is high, so a half-told line is wholly in sight in the pass drawn again, and the bottom alone could not catch it), a module folder is dropped on an open, unsaved module (`a_module_folder_dropped_on_an_open_module_is_imported`: the module stays, still modified, nothing asked, Import Resources offered), and three recent modules, the second opened by Enter and the third by Space (`a_recent_row_is_named_and_opens_by_its_keys`). **Rulings, as built**: no frame shows the strip where the page will tell the update: the first frame the page is drawn takes the line as in sight, and the page throws no pass away there (`the_first_frame_has_no_strip_and_the_page_stays`, by the count of thrown-away passes, since a thrown-away pass is never shown); what the last pass found is kept with its pass number and holds only for the next pass, so a frame where Welcome was not drawn in front leaves nothing behind (`back_on_the_page_after_a_resize_the_update_is_always_told`: every frame after coming back tells it, by the page or the strip); the strip is drawn from `updates::line`, one reading for both, so the failed state's Release Page tip is the same in both places, every state's strip otherwise as before (the words and buttons of each state checked against the tip's `notice_bar` and `install_state`, and each drawn, `strip-<state>`; the screens test `update_install` fails as before, at its What's New… click, one of the five known); the section headings (Recent Modules, Start, Status, Learn) and the sub-headings (Without a module, Help) are headings to a screen reader (`the_page_s_headings_are_headings`), and the tests take the Help menu by its place in the Top Bar and About by role; the Welcome tab's × stays out (closing it would leave an empty editor area with no way back to the page). **Smaller**: a recent row's id is its place in the list, so a hand-edited list naming a module twice has two rows, and a module with no folder is named without "in" (`a_module_named_twice_has_two_rows_and_a_bare_name_no_folder`); a dropped folder is taken for a module as the module reader takes one: a `module.ifo` in any case (a folder's files are read by `ResKey::from_filename`, which takes any case), or a nasher project's `nasher.cfg` by that very name (`nasher::Package::is_package`), and with a module open it is imported, not opened; `board_welcome` clears the log's last line as U23's board pictures do, so its Status Bar is the board's. **Probes**: Welcome in a split pane beside the Manual tells the update once, on the page, with no strip, in every frame after the split (`welcome-split-newline`); a recent module whose name holds a newline is one row high, its name cut at the newline with an ellipsis ("two…"), the whole path in its tooltip and its AccessKit name. **Deviation**: the Help menu is taken by its place in the Top Bar, not by role (egui gives a menu button the same role as the page's buttons and no menu role); User Manual and Getting started could not be taken by role either (the menu's and the page's are of the same roles): the menu's User Manual is the one whose name carries its key (F1), and Getting started stays taken by nearness. **Pictures** (Dark and Light, `target/ui-mock/impl/m4-u24-fix/`): `board_welcome` against the board (the Status Bar now as drawn), two hundred recent modules with the keys on the fortieth row past the fold, the Manual floating over the line with the strip telling it, the split pane with the newline name, the strip in each of the notice's states with the Manual in front, the page in each of its states at 1600, and No area open with and without areas; each looked at.

`Thumbnails::shown_now` counts them). **Wide layout**: with Gallery on, the Right Dock 881 and its first column 480 (`shell::RIGHT_DOCK_GALLERY`, `RIGHT_COLUMN_GALLERY`; kept widths and columns still win). **The tiles Gallery**: the model names in Hack 11 on one line and the headings' counts. **Settled**: the slider's thumb at rest (`controls::slider`'s `rail_as_well`). **Done, 2026-11-20.** **Built.** Inventoried before and after in `target/u28/inventory.txt` (nothing dropped; the one control gone is the windows' own Close, as the dock's close and Escape in a field do it). **Search Results holds one search at a time** (`search_results::Showing`: a script's lines, Find Instance's objects, Find and Replace Text's strings), its form the panel's header (`form_frame`, which scrolls in what the rows leave it at the least window, its first hit whole). Edit › Find Instance… and Find and Replace Text… (Ctrl + H) open the Bottom Dock on it with the keys in the first field (`open_find_instance`, `open_find_text`); Enter in a field searches, Escape in a field closes the dock, as it closed the window. Find Instance's hits are a table "Objects found" (`report_table::show`: Type, Tag, Area, Blueprint; heads that sort, rows in sight only, a click choosing and giving it the keys, Up, Down, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End, Enter or a double click going to the object, Ctrl + C copying the row's words); the text's strings are the board's two-line rows (tick, place link, the string under it) with the same keys and Space to tick. **The searches are jobs** (`area_tools::start_find` over an area at a time, `bulk::start_find_text` over a resource at a time, `mg_module::text::find_with`), with progress and Cancel; Search and Find are not offered while a job runs. Closing the module lets Find Instance and the text's strings go (the form kept). **Build Module per Q4(a)**: the dialog keeps its options and Build, Mark as Used (on the Unused finding chosen in Problems), Export… and Done, its note saying what went to Problems; the results and Counted as Used are **Problems'** (`problems.rs`: Build's heading, its counts said in the tab bar's place, and the Counted as Used popover where the build was asked for its Unused results, `build_view::counted_as_used`; a row's right click Mark as Used; a heading's Remove from Problems), brought to the front where anything was found. **Verify per Q5(a)**: its errors and warnings go to Problems under Verify Module's heading with their fixes (Fix, Fix All (n), Fixed), the Log keeping its lines. Both are stale as U4 built them and are taken away when the module closes. **Hak Pak Conflict Analysis, Resources Used and the Claims Table are Bottom Dock tabs** (`shell::Panel::{HakConflicts, ResourcesUsed, ClaimsTable}`, bodies in `dock_reports.rs`), opened by their commands with their table taking the keys, closed by **Close Report** (a command and the tool at the dock's tab bar end); not kept with the layout. The hak report is a job read hak by hak ("Reading hak 2 of 5", `mg_module::haks::hak_report_with`; Cancel stops it before the next hak) and its sections are views of one table (Conflicts, Overrides, All, Haks; What the Module Uses; Copy Report). **The Bottom Dock's least height** is the panel in front's form or header and its first whole row (`shell::first_row_ends`), at most half the window. **Plan against board**: one search shown at a time (decision 5 allows either); Resources Used and the Claims Table have no running state (nothing runs) and no empty state (the tab opens on what it counts); Search Results' switch counts the search shown; a chosen row of Problems and of the strings takes the tables' `accent-fill` with its words in `on-fill` (`select` is the 3D view's). **Tests** (`tests/app/dock_tabs.rs`, 18; and the moved ones in `area_view.rs`, `dialogs.rs`, `scripts.rs`, `modules.rs`, `projects.rs`, `search.rs`, `quick_open.rs`, `tileset_panels.rs`, `board_builds.rs`, `plugins.rs`; two unit tests of the searches' progress and Cancel; `dialog_pattern`'s table and openers without the five windows gone, its scan still failing when a dialog's opener is taken out; a row taken out of `every_dialog_is_listed`'s table alone did not fail it, and `the_module_dialogs_hold_the_pattern` is the guard for a missing ORDERS row), every key and action on its effect, at 50,000 rows made once and laid out only in sight; each seen to fail once with its fault put in (`target/u28/breaks.txt`). **Pictures** (`target/ui-mock/impl/m4-u28/`): the six dialogs before (the tip's) and the seven after, empty, filled, running and chosen at 1280 by 720, filled at 1600 by 900, 1280 by 720, 900 by 700 and the least window with the dock at its least and tall, Dark and Light; `board_main_problems` (`board_main` with Problems open); `build_unused_and_counted_as_used`; `u26_dialog_room` without Find and Replace Text, no longer a dialog. Three faults were seen in them and fixed: the chosen rows' fill (`select`, unreadable in Light), the least window's first hit cut under Find Instance's form (egui's least scroll height), a right click on a finding's words taking no menu (its label was selectable). **Timing** (`target/ui-mock/perf-m4/u28/`, release, interleaved with 55735616, each run begun at a load under 3): Find Instance over 50,714 found through the panel 1.54 ms a frame with the pointer moving (the tip's dialog 1.73), 1.53 at rest (1.72), 1.60 under the wheel (1.64); Build Module's 18,127 findings in Problems 1.63, 1.54 and 1.64 (the tip's dialog 2.02, 2.03, 2.07); all rest and are under the 6.94 ms budget. The two views are not alike, so the difference is not a speed-up: the dock shows fewer rows in sight than the dialog did (12,016 vertices a frame against the dialog's 15,420), and what the numbers show is that the panel costs no more than the window it replaced. **New public items** (hidden, for tests): `pub mod dock_reports` with `HakConflicts` (`new`, `order_builds`, `rows_seen`, `count`), `HakView`, `HAK_ROWS`, `USED_ROWS`, `CLAIM_ROWS`, the Claims Table's action words `RELEASE`, `HAND_TO`, `TAKE_OVER`, `CLAIM`, `ACTIONS`; `Moonglow::{show_hak_report, claims_table_counts}`, and `Moonglow::hak_report` now an `Option<dock_reports::HakConflicts>`; `search_results::{Showing, INSTANCES_FOUND, STRINGS_FOUND, instances_words}`, `SearchResults::{showing, count, instance_order_builds, instance_rows_seen, instance_chosen, form_rect, area_list_builds}`; `problems::{Problem::new, row_name, running_words, MARK_AS_USED, COUNTED_AS_USED}`, the fields `Problem::{severity, message, fix, unused}` and `Problems::build_unused`, `Problems::{retain, selected, select}`, `FILLED_BY`'s words naming Build Module and Verify Module; `build_view::UsedDraft { text, kind }`; `bulk::TextReplace::{searched, strings_seen}`; `mg_module::text::find_with`, `mg_module::haks::hak_report_with`. **Removed**: `BuildWindow::{results, selected, mark_draft, mark_kind}` (now Problems' and `UsedDraft`); `Moonglow::hak_usage` and `hak_report` as strings.

**Review, 2026-11-20.** An independent review of U28 (its evidence in `target/review-u28/`, which holds no notes file naming its B numbers: the breaks follow the orchestrator's descriptions) found the faults below; each is fixed with the orchestrator's rulings, and each new or strengthened test was seen to fail with its fault put back (`target/u28-fix/breaks.txt`: the break, the test, the failure). (10) **Find Instance's In Area list** is made as the module's change counter moves, not every frame (`SearchResults::area_list_builds`; `find_instance_s_area_list_is_made_as_the_module_changes`). (11) **The 50,000-row tests count what is drawn** (AccessKit nodes with a box), not a record the code keeps; they failed with 200 rows laid out past those in sight. (12) Resources Used's icon is `Icon::Statistics`. (13) **The hak header**: the segmented control alone at the left, What the Module Uses and Copy Report set apart (`the_hak_report_s_buttons_stand_apart_from_its_view_switch`). Of the ruling's two ways (each view setting a fixed camera, or `view_in` restoring it) this is a third, U30's choice: it keeps the later views timed from where they were before U6, so that their rows compare with the parent's; they still inherit each other's camera, as they always have. Timed at the tip, three rounds, each at a load under 3 (`target/ui-mock/perf-m4/u30/fix-round/table.txt`), the five rows' medians are 5.2 to 6.3 ms, under the budget: up to half a millisecond above the reviewer's runs of U6's parent (a60f8b56, A1 to A6: 4.6 to 5.9 on those rows, one disturbed run aside) and within those of U6 without its panel views (N1 to N4), on another night. #### Rulings for M4

Five choices the boards, the proposal and the earlier rulings leave open, each with a recommendation and the task it gates. A task before its gate does not depend on the answer.

- **Q1. A double click on a placed object.** Today it opens the object's Properties as a tab or window with OK and Cancel (area_view.rs:5553-5559). The Main and Floating boards draw the Properties panel in both modes, but ruling 1 of the second set promises an existing builder no window changed by an update. (a) A double click shows the Properties panel and brings it to the front, unfolding the Right Dock, in both modes; Open in Tab and the context menu's Properties… open today's tab or window. (b) As (a) As Tabs, but As Floating Windows a double click keeps opening the window. **Recommended: (a).** The panel applies at once as the window already does (its Cancel is one Undo step), the window stays one click away, and ruling 1 is about where editors open, not where a placed object's fields are. Gates U6. **Ruled by the owner, 2026-11-14: (a), as recommended.**
- **Q2. The module tree's area rows (R2's remainder).** The boards' Module panel lists areas without arrows. (a) Keep them, as T13's ruling left the tree (it keeps an area opened out when the builder opens it, and follows the selection only while no Outliner shows). (b) Remove them: the Outliner shows the area in front. **Recommended: (a)**: the objects of an area not in front are reachable only there, nothing disappears, and the boards simply show no area opened. Gates U6. **Ruled by the owner, 2026-11-14: (a), as recommended.**
- **Q3. Plugin panels (R3, to be revisited "when the dialogs become panels in M4").** (a) Tabs or windows, following the Open editors switch, as R3 built them. (b) Right Dock panels. **Recommended: (a)**: they are no one editor's, and the Right Dock follows the active editor, so a plugin's panel would come and go with the tab in front. Gates U29. **Ruled by the owner, 2026-11-14: (a), as recommended.**
- **Q4. Build Module, between the dialog and Problems.** Ruling 5 sends its results to Problems; the Dialogs board draws Build Module whole as a dialog. (a) The dialog keeps its options and Build, Mark as Used, Export… and Done; its Results and Counted as Used move to Problems, which Build opens. (b) The options become a Bottom Dock panel beside Problems too. (c) As the board: results stay in the dialog. **Recommended: (a)**: it keeps the board's dialog and the ruling's Problems, and results are what is worked through after the dialog is closed. Gates U28. **Ruled by the owner, 2026-11-14: (a), as recommended.**
- **Q5. Verify's findings in Problems.** Today Verify writes its findings to the log, with fixes beside them (09-build-verify-test, "Verify Module"). (a) They also go to Problems, with their fixes, the log keeping its lines. (b) Problems holds Build Module's results and the tileset's Check alone. **Recommended: (a)**: the Problems switch's badge reads as the module's problems, and Verify's are the main ones; but section 14 lists no such feature, so it is the owner's. Gates U28. **Ruled by the owner, 2026-11-14: (a), as recommended.**

The NUI review's line reference is left, being pinned to its commit. **Independent review** (`target/review-m5-S1/`), faults fixed. Whole suite 5104 passed, 0 failed.

### M6. The viewer

- The viewer moves to the toolset release's tag and takes `mg-uikit`, the shell and the look; the copied helpers go.
- Its renames (Nodes to Outliner, Animation to Timeline, the View menu names) and Gallery mode for Resources, with **its manual updated in the same change**.
- Exit: the viewer's boards (Model with ASCII Editor, Creature and Colors, 3440 by 1440, Gallery) reproduced in pictures; frame time measured.

**Kit parts for the viewer, 2026-11-25.** What the viewer would otherwise copy from `mg-ui` is in `mg-uikit`, and the toolset runs on it: the docks' stacks (`mg_uikit::stack`: the arrangement, the drops among one dock or several, the sections' heights and seams, the record kept for a kind), the galleries' picture bookkeeping (`mg_uikit::pictures`, without threads or GPU: each application reads and draws its own), a panel header's badges and the document tab's close button (`shell`). The toolset keeps its panels in their own dock; moving one between docks is the viewer's to turn on.

## 17. Open for the owner

Nothing in the design is open. Two things are the owner's by custom: ruling 7 (Ubuntu Light) is judged after M2, and each release is signed by the owner (M5, M6).
